definition_zh: 说服；劝使（某人做某事）；打动并争取过来
definition_en: to cause someone to accept a belief or to take an action by giving reasons or by winning them over
core_image: 一间小屋里，散乱的证词被摆成一条直线，听者沿着线走到说话人站的结论处
scene: 答辩室里，年轻讲师把一页图表推到委员面前，零散的数据连成一条能读下去的线。A single clear chart helped the young lecturer persuade the skeptical committee to fund the project.
sceneCN: 这里 persuade 指「用理由使人接受某个结论」（第 1 个义项：以论证令听者信服）；句意为一张清晰的图表让这位年轻讲师说服了原本怀疑的委员会为该项目拨款。可辨识物件：投影幕、图表、水杯、委员的名牌。

collocations.phrase: persuade somebody out of a decision
collocations.zh: 劝某人改掉已定的主意

senses.title: Make someone accept a conclusion
senses.titleCN: 以论证使人接受某个结论
senses.definition: to cause a person to believe that something is true by presenting reasons
senses.definitionCN: 通过摆出理由，使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The report persuaded the board that the old warehouse could be converted.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告使董事会相信，那座旧仓库可以改造。
senses.why: the oldest layer of the word is advice: per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'to advise' yields 'advise until the point is carried'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「进言」：per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」，合起来就是「劝到对方接受为止」。

senses.title: Urge someone to act
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something they might not otherwise do
senses.definitionCN: 劝得某人去做他本不一定会做的事
senses.example: She persuaded her brother to take the later train.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服弟弟改乘晚一班火车。
senses.why: once the listener accepts the reasons, the next step is to move: advice about an act becomes advice to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 听者接受理由之后，下一步就是行动：关于「该怎么做」的进言，自然变成「去做」的劝使。

senses.title: Succeed where others failed
senses.titleCN: 把原本不肯的一方争取过来
senses.definition: to win over someone who has resisted argument, so that the attempt succeeds
senses.definitionCN: 把一直抗拒说理的一方争取过来，使劝说真正成功
senses.example: After two hours of argument he finally persuaded the holdouts.
senses.exampleCN: 争辩了两个小时，他终于说服了那几个坚持不让步的人。
senses.why: modern English treats persuade as a success verb: to say you persuaded someone is to say the person yielded.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把 persuade 当作「结果动词」：说「说服了某人」，就等于说对方已经让步。

senses.title: Win someone over by feeling
senses.titleCN: 靠情感打动而争取过来
senses.definition: to gain a person's agreement through warmth, charm or emotional appeal rather than proof
senses.definitionCN: 不靠证明，而以温情、魅力或情感打动来取得对方同意
senses.example: The singer's account persuaded even the reporters who had come to sneer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手的讲述甚至打动了本来打算嘲弄她的记者。
senses.why: suadere is generally thought to be tied to suavis 'sweet', so the word has always carried a hint of pleasantness as well as argument.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关，因此这个词除了论理，一直带着一点「可亲、顺耳」的意味。

senses.title: Come to believe after hearing
senses.titleCN: 被动义：听过之后转而相信
senses.definition: to become convinced of something oneself, especially in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 自己听过之后转为相信，多见于被动结构
senses.example: I was persuaded by the data, not by the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 让我信服的是数据，那番演讲并没有说服我。
senses.why: when the verb is passive, the listener moves to the side of the speaker, and the action is viewed from the receiving end.
senses.whyCN: 用于被动时，听者移到说话人这一边，动作便从「接受的一方」来看。

senses.title: Advise or urge strongly
senses.definition: to urge or advise a course of action forcefully, without implying that the advice was taken
senses.definitionCN: 强烈敦促或建议某种做法，不含「已被采纳」之意
senses.example: The old manuals persuade the reader to test each joint twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这些旧手册力劝读者把每个接缝都测两遍。
senses.why: seventeenth-century English used persuade where modern English would say urge; the success reading only became fixed later.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪的英语在今天的 urge 之处用 persuade；「成功」这层读法是后来才固定的。

senses.title: Talk oneself into believing
senses.definition: to bring oneself to accept something uncomfortable or doubtful
senses.definitionCN: 让自己接受某种令人不安或未必可靠的事
senses.example: He persuaded himself that the delay was harmless.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服自己相信这次延误并无妨碍。
senses.why: the mind can play both roles, speaker and listener, so the verb turns reflexive and describes inner bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 头脑可以同时扮演说话人与听者，于是这个动词转为自反，描述内心里的讨价还价。

senses.title: Swing a group as a whole
senses.definition: to change the decision of a body or assembly rather than a single person
senses.definitionCN: 使一个机构或集会整体改变决定，而非只改变一个人
senses.example: The petition persuaded the council to reopen the footpath.
senses.exampleCN: 请愿书使议会重新开放那条步道。
senses.why: a council votes as one voice, so persuading it means shifting the majority inside it.
senses.whyCN: 议会按一个声音投票，因此说服议会，实际上就是让其中的多数改向。

senses.title: Win people to a cause
senses.titleCN: 使人归附某种信念或事业
senses.definition: to convert people to a faith, party or cause one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个把人争取到某种信仰、党派或事业这一边
senses.example: Missionaries persuaded villagers one household at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 传教士一家一家地把村民争取过来。
senses.why: the same winning-over gesture, repeated person by person, becomes the language of conversion and recruitment.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「争取过来」的动作，一个人一个人地重复，就成了皈依与招纳的说法。

intro.en: Persuade entered English from Latin persuadere 'to urge thoroughly, prevail upon', built on per- 'thoroughly' and suadere 'to advise, urge'. Suadere is generally thought to be related to suavis 'sweet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persuade 从拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」进入英语，由 per-「彻底」与 suadere「劝告、敦促」构成。一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Suadere meant 'to advise, recommend, urge'. The connection with suavis 'sweet, pleasant' is generally thought to be genuine, but the similarity alone does not prove it, and any deeper Indo-European shape for it exists only as a reconstructed form.
items.cn: suadere 意为「劝告、推荐、敦促」。它与 suavis「甜的、可亲的」的联系一般认为是真实的，但仅凭音形相近不足以证明；为它构拟的更早印欧形式只以重构形式存在。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere produced persuadere, 'to advise thoroughly, to prevail upon, to convince'. The prefix turns a piece of advice into an action carried through.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere 构成 persuadere，意为「劝到底、争取过来、使信服」。这个前缀把一句劝告变成一个做到底的动作。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the late fourteenth century, either taken straight from Latin or through Middle French persuader.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪晚期出现于英语，或直接取自拉丁语，或经中古法语 persuader 传入。

items.en: Early modern English still used the word for plain urging, where a modern writer would choose urge or advise; no success was implied.
items.cn: 早期现代英语仍用它表示单纯的「力劝」，今天的写作者会改用 urge 或 advise；当时并不含成功之意。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the success reading had settled in, and the passive 'be persuaded' became the ordinary way to report a change of mind.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「劝说成功」的读法已经固定，被动式「被说服」成为报告改变想法的常说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and deeper origin): the earliest dated example varies between dictionaries, and every pre-Latin form offered for suadere is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证与更深来源）：各家词典给出的最早年代并不一致；凡为 suadere 提出的拉丁语之前形式，都是重构形式，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look or sound close to persuade, one of which is not related at the root at all; group two gathers verbs that also move a listener but with a different lever.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，其中一个在词根上与本词毫无关系；第二组收同样能推动听者、但所用杠杆不同的动词。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus suadere, so it means to advise someone away from an action, the mirror image of persuade.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「离开」加 suadere，意为劝人不要做某事，正是 persuade 的镜像。

entries.definition: From Old French assouagier, from a Latin stem built on suavis 'sweet': to soften or soothe pain, sharing the sweet root but not the advising root.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语 assouagier，出自以 suavis「甜的」为基的拉丁词干：减轻、抚慰痛苦；与「甜」同根，却不走「劝告」这一支。

entries.tag: rare noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The formal noun from Latin suasio 'a advising', now mostly confined to the phrase moral suasion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 suasio「劝告」的正式名词，如今基本只用于「道义劝告」这一说法。

entries.definition: From Latin prosequi 'follow after', built on sequi 'to follow'; it looks close to persuade but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 prosequi「跟随」，由 sequi「跟随」构成；字形与 persuade 相近，词根却毫无关系。

entries.definition: To bring someone to accept a fact as true; the emphasis is on belief rather than on action.
entries.definitionCN: 使人接受某事实为真；侧重「相信」，而非「行动」。

entries.definition: To obtain something by gentle, patient urging; there is no argument, only smooth persistence.
entries.definitionCN: 靠温和耐心的劝哄取得某物；不讲道理，只靠柔和的坚持。

entries.definition: To influence a crowd or a decision, often through emotion; it is weaker on proof than persuade.
entries.definitionCN: 影响人群或决定，常借情感；在「论证」上比 persuade 弱。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for getting someone to agree by persistent asking, common in letters and speeches.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的「恳请」说法，靠一再请求使人同意，多见于书信与演说。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'advise': advice carried all the way through.
normal.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」：把劝告做到底。

normal.en: The family runs persuade, persuasion, persuasive, persuasively, persuasiveness, persuader.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persuade、persuasion、persuasive、persuasively、persuasiveness、persuader。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the two objects: persuade somebody to act, persuade somebody of a fact.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出两类宾语：劝人去做、使人相信某事实。

normal.en: The reverse verb is dissuade, built with the prefix that means apart.
normal.cn: 反向的动词是 dissuade，由表示「离开」的前缀构成。

normal.en: Passive reports are common: the committee was persuaded, the jury was persuaded.
normal.cn: 被动说法很常见：委员会被说服、陪审团被说服。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door that opens only after every key has been tried in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门，只有按顺序试过每一把钥匙才会开。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that tips only when a pebble is added to one side.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，只有在一侧再加一粒小石子时才倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a listener walking along a rope the speaker has laid out.
abstract.cn: 想象听者沿着说话人铺好的绳子往前走。

examples.en: Nothing could persuade the old farmer to sell the orchard.
examples.cn: 什么也无法说服那位老农卖掉果园。

examples.en: The teacher persuaded the class that the experiment was worth repeating.
examples.cn: 老师让全班相信这个实验值得重做一遍。

examples.en: He was persuaded only after he had read the original letters.
examples.cn: 他读过原始信件之后才被说服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（彻底）+ suade（劝）」——一直劝到对方彻底点头 → 说服

root: 拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」= per-（彻底）+ suadere「劝告、敦促」；suadere 与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是同源，更深印欧形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: reasons are laid out, the listener is urged, belief settles, and belief turns into action or into a whole group changing course.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：先摆出理由，再向听者进言，信念落定，最后信念转为行动，或转为整群人改向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of reasons laid out on a table, along which a doubtful listener walks to the speaker's side.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上铺开一条理由的线，心存怀疑的听者沿着它走到说话人一边。

branches.en: ADVICE COMPLETED: the oldest layer is urging and advising, carried through to the end.
branches.cn: 把劝告做到底：最古老的一层是敦促与进言，一直做到终点。

branches.en: ACTION AND ASSEMBLY: a single listener is moved to act, then a whole council is moved to change course.
branches.cn: 行动与全体：先推动一个听者去做，再推动整个议会改向。

branches.en: BELIEF SURRENDERED: the resisting mind yields, and the passive form reports the change from the receiving side.
branches.cn: 信念让步：抗拒的一方松手，被动式则从接受方报告这一变化。

branches.en: SWEET PRESSURE: charm and warmth do the work that proof cannot do.
branches.cn: 甜的推力：证明做不到的事，由魅力与温情做到。

branches.en: INNER AND OUTER CONVERSION: the same voice persuades oneself, or persuades a household at a time.
branches.cn: 向内向外的皈依：同一个声音，可以劝服自己，也可以一家一家地劝服。

intro.en: Persuade is a Latin verb whose prefix and root still build English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: persuade 是一个拉丁动词，其前缀与词根至今仍在构成英语词，因此整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin suadere gives persuade, dissuade, suasion and assuage; the prefix per- adds the sense of doing something thoroughly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suadere 衍生 persuade、dissuade、suasion 与 assuage；前缀 per- 增添「彻底」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks the advice as carried through to success.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把关切标记为一直做到成功。

items.example: The root contributes the whole idea of advising.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贡献了「劝告」的全部意思。

items.example: The chart persuaded the committee.
items.exampleCN: 那张图表说服了委员会。

items.example: A neighbour dissuaded him from signing.
items.exampleCN: 一位邻居劝他不要签字。

items.meaning: the act or result of persuading
items.example: The argument needed no further persuasion.
items.exampleCN: 这个论点无需再作说服。

items.example: She wrote a persuasive letter to the editor.
items.exampleCN: 她给编辑写了一封有说服力的信。

items.example: He argued persuasively for a second trial.
items.exampleCN: 他有力地为再次试验辩护。

items.example: The persuasiveness of the data surprised the panel.
items.exampleCN: 数据之有说服力让评审组意外。

items.example: Dissuasion worked better than punishment.
items.exampleCN: 劝阻比惩罚更有效。

items.example: The campaign relied on moral suasion.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动依靠道义劝告。

definition_zh: 有说服力的；能打动人心的；令人信服的
definition_en: able to make a person believe something or agree to act, or having the quality that wins people over
core_image: 一句话落到桌面，原本摇头的人把椅子向前挪了半寸
scene: 会议室里，一位年轻人只讲了三分钟，原本交抱双臂的经理们开始翻看方案。Her persuasive summary turned a room of doubtful managers into supporters within three minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 persuasive 指「论证足以让人改变判断，并愿意跟着行动」（第 1 个义项：使人信服的力量）；句意为她那段有说服力的总结，让满屋子原本怀疑的经理在三分钟内变成了支持者。可辨识物件：投影仪、会议桌、摊开的方案、半杯咖啡。

pos.zh: 有说服力的；能打动人的

collocations.zh: 为某事提出的有力理由

senses.title: Convincing to the mind
senses.definition: of an argument or a case, strong enough to make a reasonable listener accept it
senses.definitionCN: 指论证或理由足够有力，使通情理的听者接受
senses.example: The report made a persuasive case for restoring the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为恢复那片沼泽提出了有力的理由。
senses.why: the adjective simply names the power that the verb describes: what can persuade is persuasive.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给动词所描述的那种力量命名：能说服人的，就是「有说服力的」。

senses.title: Effective in moving people to act
senses.titleCN: 能促使人真的行动起来
senses.definition: of a text or a campaign, able to produce action and not only agreement
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或活动不仅使人同意，还能促成实际行动
senses.example: A persuasive poster cut household water use by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 一张有说服力的海报让家庭用水减少了五分之一。
senses.why: persuading has always ended in an act in English, so the adjective inherits that push toward doing.
senses.whyCN: 英语里的 persuade 一向以「行动」收尾，因此这个形容词也继承了那股推向行动的力量。

senses.title: Skilled at winning others over
senses.titleCN: 指人善于把别人争取过来
senses.definition: of a person, habitually able to make others agree with him or her
senses.definitionCN: 指某人一贯能把别人说得同意自己
senses.example: She is the most persuasive member of the negotiating team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是谈判小组里最善于说服人的成员。
senses.why: the quality moves from the argument to the person who habitually produces such arguments.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质从「论证」移到了「惯常做出这种论证的人」身上。

senses.title: Winning in manner
senses.titleCN: 举止动人、令人乐于亲近
senses.definition: of a smile, voice or manner, pleasing in a way that makes people willing
senses.definitionCN: 指笑容、声音或举止讨人喜欢，使人愿意应允
senses.example: His persuasive smile opened doors that argument could not.
senses.exampleCN: 他那动人的笑容打开了论证打不开的门。
senses.why: the old link between the root and sweetness survives in this sense, where charm replaces reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 词根与「甜」的古老联系在这一义项里留存下来：魅力取代了论理。

senses.title: Apparently sound but unproven
senses.definition: of an explanation, plausible enough to be tempting although the evidence stops short of proof
senses.definitionCN: 指某种解释颇有道理、引人相信，但证据尚不足以证明
senses.example: The correlation is persuasive but far from conclusive.
senses.exampleCN: 这项相关性颇有说服力，却远未成为定论。
senses.why: English often marks the gap between sounding convincing and being true, and persuasive sits exactly on that line.
senses.whyCN: 英语常区分「听着可信」与「确实为真」，而 persuasive 正落在这条线上。

senses.title: Forceful and vivid in style
senses.definition: of writing or speech, carrying the reader along through force and clear images
senses.definitionCN: 指文章或言辞以力量与清晰的意象把读者带着走
senses.example: The essay is persuasive because every image is sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章有力，是因为每个意象都鲜明。
senses.why: style persuades by making the reader see, so the word came to describe craft as well as logic.
senses.whyCN: 文风靠让读者看见来说服，于是这个词也用来描述写作手艺，而不只描述逻辑。

senses.title: Strong enough to overcome doubt
senses.definition: of an answer or a reason, weighty enough to quiet a specific doubt
senses.definitionCN: 指回答或理由足够有分量，能压住具体的疑虑
senses.example: No persuasive answer came from the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 部里没有给出一个足以释疑的答复。
senses.why: this sense measures the adjective against a particular objection rather than against truth in general.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项衡量的是它能否压住某个具体反对意见，而不是一般意义上的真假。

senses.title: Enough to sway a jury
senses.definition: of evidence in law, sufficient to move a court or jury toward a finding
senses.definitionCN: 指法律上的证据足以使法院或陪审团倾向于某一认定
senses.example: The defence called the fingerprint match persuasive.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方称那处指纹吻合具有说服力。
senses.why: courts need a word for evidence that convinces without being conclusive, and this adjective fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要一个词来形容「足以令人信服但不必 conclusive」的证据，这个形容词正好补上这个位置。

intro.en: Persuasive is persuade plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus, which reached English through Old French -if. It names the quality of what can persuade.
intro.cn: persuasive 是 persuade 加上拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus，该词尾经古法语 -if 进入英语。它命名的是「能说服人」这种性质。

items.en: The root suadere 'to advise, urge' supplies the meaning; its link with suavis 'sweet' is generally thought to be real but is not provable from the words alone.
items.cn: 词根 suadere「劝告、敦促」提供词义；它与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是真实的，但仅凭这两个词无法证明。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere gave persuadere, 'to prevail upon', the verb behind the adjective.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere 得出 persuadere「争取过来」，即这个形容词背后的动词。

items.en: The ending -ivus marked a quality or a tendency, as in actus and activus; English took it through the French form -if.
items.cn: 词尾 -ivus 表示性质或倾向，如 actus 与 activus；英语经法语形式 -if 接受它。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the late sixteenth century, first of speeches and arguments, later of persons.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪晚期见于英语，最初用于演说与论证，后来才用于人。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it spread to advertising, statistics and law, wherever a claim has to carry a listener along.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，它扩展到广告、统计与法律，凡是一个主张需要带动听者的地方都用得上。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries differ by a few years on the earliest citation, and no attested pre-Latin form of the root exists, so deeper shapes are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对最早书证的年代相差数年；该词根在拉丁语之前没有有书证的形式，更深的形式均为重构。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that look close on the page but come from three different Latin verbs; group two holds adjectives that also move a listener, each with a different strength.
note.cn: 第一组收纸面上形近、却出自三个不同拉丁动词的形容词；第二组收同样能推动听者、但力道不同的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin pervadere 'spread through', built on vadere 'to go'; it means spreading everywhere, with no connection to advising.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pervadere「蔓延穿过」，由 vadere「走」构成；意为遍布各处，与「劝告」无关。

entries.definition: From permittere 'let through', built on mittere 'to send'; it means allowing rather than convincing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 permittere「放行」，由 mittere「送」构成；意为容许，而非说服。

entries.definition: The mirror adjective, built on dis- plus suadere: tending to advise someone away from an act.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像形容词，由 dis- 加 suadere 构成：倾向于劝人不要做某事。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the resulting belief; it is the base from which the adjective is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 表示行为或由此形成的信念的名词；正是构成这个形容词的基础。

entries.definition: Able to remove doubt about a fact; it leans on evidence where persuasive leans on the effect on the hearer.
entries.definitionCN: 能消除对某事实的怀疑；偏重证据，而 persuasive 偏重对听者的作用。

entries.definition: So forceful that attention and assent are almost forced; stronger and less polite than persuasive.
entries.definitionCN: 强到几乎迫使注意与赞同；比 persuasive 更重，也更不容气。

entries.definition: Of an argument, tightly reasoned and hard to answer; it praises structure rather than charm.
entries.definitionCN: 指论证严密、难以反驳；赞的是结构，不是魅力。

entries.definition: Moving through beautiful or forceful language; eloquent speech may persuade, but the word describes the speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 以优美或有力的言辞打动人；动人的话固然可能说服人，但这个词描述的是「说得漂亮」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the verb plus the Latin quality ending -ive, so it means 'having the power to persuade'.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是动词加拉丁性质词尾 -ive，意为「具有说服的力量」。

normal.en: The family runs persuade, persuasion, persuasive, persuasively, persuasiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persuade、persuasion、persuasive、persuasively、persuasiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep it next to speech and evidence: a persuasive speech, persuasive evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与言辞、证据放在一起：有感染力的演讲、令人信服的证据。

normal.en: The negative form is unpersuasive, used of weak cases and flat writing.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unpersuasive，用于薄弱的理由与平淡的文字。

normal.en: The reverse adjective is dissuasive, the mirror of this one.
normal.cn: 反向的形容词是 dissuasive，正好是本词的镜像。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that rests lightly on a door and the door gives way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻放在门上，门就顺势开了。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp placed where everyone in the room must walk toward it.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯放在全屋人都不得不朝它走的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut so exactly that the lock turns on the first try.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙削得极准，第一下就把锁转开了。

examples.en: A persuasive letter can change a landlord's mind faster than a threat.
examples.cn: 一封有说服力的信，比一句威胁更快让房东改变主意。

examples.en: The lawyer built a persuasive narrative out of three ordinary facts.
examples.cn: 律师用三件平常的事实搭出一个令人信服的叙述。

examples.en: Her voice was quiet but persuasive in the crowded hall.
examples.cn: 在拥挤的大厅里，她的声音不高，却很有说服力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（彻底）+ suas（劝）+ ive（性质）」——劝到底的那种劲 → 有说服力的

root: 拉丁 persuasivus = per-（彻底）+ suadere（劝告）+ -ivus（性质词尾）；suadere 与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses ask one question in different places: how much carrying power does this argument, person, smile, style or piece of evidence actually have?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同场合问同一个问题：这段论证、这个人、这个笑容、这种文风或这份证据，究竟有多少带动人的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence laid on a table that makes a doubtful listener lean forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句落在桌面的话，让心存怀疑的听者把身子往前倾。

branches.en: CASES AND ANSWERS: a case is weighed, and a specific doubt is measured against it.
branches.cn: 理由与答复：一边称量理由是否成立，一边衡量它能否压住具体疑虑。

branches.en: FROM AGREEMENT TO ACTION: a poster changes behaviour, and evidence moves a jury toward a finding.
branches.cn: 从同意到行动：海报改变行为，证据推动陪审团走向某一认定。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same power is located first in skill, then in charm of manner.
branches.cn: 人本身：同一种力量先落在「技巧」上，再落到举止的魅力上。

branches.en: THE UNPROVEN: what merely sounds sound sits on the line between plausible and proven.
branches.cn: 未经证实者：只是「听着有理」的东西，正停在「可信」与「已证」之间。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: clear images and force of phrasing persuade without a single formal argument.
branches.cn: 写作手艺：鲜明的意象与有力的措辞，不必有一个正式论证也能说服人。

intro.en: Persuasive is built from a Latin verb plus a Latin quality ending, and both parts recur across English.
intro.cn: persuasive 由一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁性质词尾构成，两部分在英语中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin suadere gives persuade and dissuade, while -ivus gives a large family of English adjectives such as active and effective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suadere 衍生 persuade 与 dissuade，而 -ivus 衍生出 active、effective 等一大批英语形容词。

items.example: The prefix marks advice carried to its end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「劝到终点」。

items.example: The root carries the advising idea.
items.exampleCN: 词根带着「劝告」的意思。

items.example: The ending turns a verb into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成一种性质。

items.example: Her summary was persuasive.
items.exampleCN: 她的总结有说服力。

items.example: He spoke persuasively about the risk.
items.exampleCN: 他有力地谈到了这项风险。

items.example: The persuasiveness of her case won the vote.
items.exampleCN: 她理由的说服力赢下了表决。

items.example: The excuse sounded unpersuasive.
items.exampleCN: 那个借口听起来没有说服力。

items.example: The fine had a dissuasive effect.
items.exampleCN: 这笔罚款起了劝阻作用。

items.example: Persuasion failed and the vote was called.
items.exampleCN: 说服失败，于是付诸表决。

definition_zh: 谈判；协商；谈成；穿过（险处）；兑现或转让（票据）
definition_en: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement, or to get past a difficulty, a stretch of ground or a financial instrument
core_image: 两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，谁都没有停下，却都过去了
scene: 长桌两端各坐三人，条款被逐条划掉又改写，最后只剩两行。The two firms met for a third day to negotiate the terms of the supply contract.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiate 指「为达成一致而反复商谈」（第 1 个义项：双方就条件来回商量）；句意为两家公司第三天再聚，就供货合同的条款进行谈判。可辨识物件：长桌、两份合同、钢笔、冷掉的茶。

pos.zh: 谈成（条件）；顺利通过（险处）；兑现（票据）

senses.title: Discuss in order to agree
senses.titleCN: 为达成一致而反复商谈
senses.definition: to talk with another party, trading proposals, until a shared position is reached
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方来回提出方案，直到达成共同的立场
senses.example: Union and management negotiated for eleven hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与资方谈了十一个小时。
senses.why: the Latin source means carrying on business, and bargaining is business conducted in words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「做买卖」，而讨价还价正是用言语做的买卖。

senses.title: Settle the terms of a deal
senses.definition: to settle a price, a contract or a release by bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价把价格、合同或释放条件定下来
senses.example: The captain negotiated the release of the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 船长谈成了船员的释放。
senses.why: the verb shifts from the talking to its product: what has been agreed now exists as terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从「谈」转向「谈出的结果」：已议定之事，如今作为条款存在。

senses.title: Get past a difficulty
senses.definition: to deal with an obstacle or a stage of a process successfully
senses.definitionCN: 成功地应付一处障碍或某个程序阶段
senses.example: The bill negotiated the committee stage intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案完整地通过了委员会阶段。
senses.why: a difficulty is treated like a stretch of road: you do not remove it, you get through it.
senses.whyCN: 难题被当成一段路来看：你不拆掉它，而是穿过去。

senses.title: Cross rough ground
senses.definition: to travel over or through a difficult physical passage
senses.definitionCN: 从一段难走的实际通道上通过
senses.example: Mules negotiate the narrow ledge without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 骡子毫不犹豫地走过那道窄石檐。
senses.why: this is the most physical branch: the bargaining skill of finding a way through becomes walking through.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的一支：谈判中「找出一条路」的本事，变成了真的走过去。

senses.title: Transfer or cash a draft
senses.definition: of a cheque or bill, to pass it to another party for value
senses.definitionCN: 指支票或汇票被交给另一方以取得对价
senses.example: The bank refused to negotiate the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝兑付这张汇票。
senses.why: a bill of exchange is a promise passed from hand to hand, and the verb names that passing.
senses.whyCN: 汇票是一张在人与人之间传递的承诺，这个动词命名的正是这次传递。

senses.title: Carry on trade
senses.definition: to buy and sell, to conduct business, in the older commercial sense
senses.definitionCN: 买卖货物、经营生意，属较早的商业用法
senses.example: Merchants negotiated in spices and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们在香料与锡之间做买卖。
senses.why: the original Latin verb meant exactly this; the diplomatic sense is the later narrowing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原动词正是这个意思；后来外交上的用法才是收窄出来的。

senses.title: Obtain by bargaining
senses.definition: to secure a benefit for oneself or others through bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价为自己或他人争得某种好处
senses.example: She negotiated a shorter working week for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她为整个团队争得了更短的工作周。
senses.why: negotiating is not only meeting the other side halfway; it is also extracting a concession from them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判不只是各让一步，也是从对方那里争得一项让步。

senses.title: Manage a passage successfully
senses.definition: to handle a vehicle or a situation through a hazardous passage
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆或局面稳稳地带过一段危险路程
senses.example: The pilot negotiated the storm with steady hands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员稳稳地把飞机带过了暴风雨。
senses.why: when the obstacle is weather or traffic, the word describes control rather than talking.
senses.whyCN: 当障碍是天气或车流时，这个词描述的是「掌控」，而不是「商谈」。

intro.en: Negotiate comes from Latin negotiari 'to carry on business', from negotium 'business', literally 'not-leisure'. The agreement sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiate 来自拉丁 negotiari「做买卖」，其名词 negotium「事务、生意」字面是「不得闲」。表示「达成协议」的义项是后来收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business, affair' was formed from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure': business is the state in which one has no leisure.
items.cn: negotium「事务、生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成：生意就是「不得闲」的状态。

items.en: The deponent verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business, to trade', and negotiator named the merchant who did so.
items.cn: 异态动词 negotiari 意为「经营、买卖」，negotiatio 与 negotiator 分别指经商这件事与经商的商人。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century first in the commercial sense of trading and dealing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初正是「做买卖、经营」的商业义。

items.en: The sense of conferring with someone, talking a matter over, appears next, still without any promise of agreement.
items.cn: 接着出现「与人商议、把事情谈一谈」的义项，当时仍不含达成协议的承诺。

items.en: Diplomacy fixed the modern sense: to confer with a view to reaching terms, and later to settle those terms.
items.cn: 外交用法固定了现代义：为议定条件而商谈，后来又指把这些条件谈成。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the boundary between the conferring sense and the settling sense is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the earlier history of otium beyond Latin is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对「商议」与「谈成」两义的分界年代说法不一；otium 在拉丁语之前的来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the shape of the ending but come from unrelated Latin verbs; group two holds verbs that also settle matters between people.
note.cn: 第一组收词尾形状相同、却出自互不相干的拉丁动词的词；第二组收同样在人与人之间把事定下来的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin negare 'to deny', built on neg- 'not'; it means to deny or make ineffective, with no link to business.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 negare「否认」，由 neg-「不」构成；意为否定或使失效，与「生意」无关。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare, built on navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive'; it means to steer a course, not to bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare，由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成；意为掌舵行船，而非讨价还价。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same verb: open to being discussed, or able to be transferred.
entries.definitionCN: 同出于这个动词的形容词：可以商量的，或可以转让的。

entries.definition: The prefixed form: to open the terms of an agreement again and bargain them afresh.
entries.definitionCN: 加前缀的形式：重新打开已达成的条件再谈一遍。

entries.definition: To argue over price or terms in a market; it is the everyday, usually smaller-scale word.
entries.definitionCN: 在市场上为价格或条件争来讲去；是日常、通常规模较小的说法。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them agree; the mediator may not be a party to the deal.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间帮助他们达成一致；调停者本身可能并非交易的一方。

entries.definition: To arrange a deal between others, often for a fee; the broker acts on behalf of the parties.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人安排交易，常收取费用；经纪人代表当事人行事。

entries.definition: To bring a dispute to an end and fix the terms; it names the closing moment rather than the talking.
entries.definitionCN: 把争端结束并定下条件；命名的是收尾那一刻，而不是商谈过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure': business is literally the opposite of free time.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」：生意字面上就是「没有闲功夫」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with contracts and prices: negotiate a contract, negotiate a price.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与合同、价格配在一起：协商合同、商议价格。

normal.en: The same verb crosses obstacles: negotiate a bend, negotiate the narrow ledge.
normal.cn: 同一个动词也用于越过障碍：通过弯道、走过窄石檐。

normal.en: Banks negotiate drafts, so the word appears in finance as well as diplomacy.
normal.cn: 银行会兑付汇票，因此这个词既在外交也在金融里出现。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one table through a narrow door, each tilting his own end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张桌子过窄门，各抬自己那一头并各自倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from both banks until it is taut but not broken.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳从两岸同时收紧，绷直却没有断。

abstract.en: Picture a path that exists only where two sets of footprints overlap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只存在于两串脚印重合处的路。

examples.en: The two governments negotiated for months before signing anything.
examples.cn: 两国政府在签字之前谈了好几个月。

examples.en: He negotiated a lower rent by offering to repair the roof himself.
examples.cn: 他提出自己修屋顶，以此谈低了房租。

examples.en: The old road negotiates the cliff in a series of tight turns.
examples.cn: 那条老路用一连串急弯绕过悬崖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ne（不）+ goti（闲）+ ate」——不得闲，就得去谈生意 → 谈判

root: 拉丁 negotiari「经商」出自 negotium「事务、生意」= neg-（不）+ otium（闲暇）；「谈成协议」义为后世收窄而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from business as the opposite of leisure: people talk terms, terms harden into a deal, and the same knack of getting through is then applied to obstacles, ground, storm and paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「生意即不得闲」出发：人们先谈条件，条件凝成交易，随后同一套「过得去」的本事被用于障碍、地形、风暴与票据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two boats in a narrow channel each give half a rudder and both pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，双方都过去了。

branches.en: TALKING INTO TERMS: proposals move between the parties until a deal exists.
branches.cn: 谈出条款：方案在双方之间来回，直到交易成形。

branches.en: CONTROLLED PASSAGE: a bill or an aircraft is brought through a hard stretch without damage.
branches.cn: 稳妥通过：法案或飞机被稳稳带过一段难走的路。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND COMMERCIAL ROOT: crossing ground and trading goods are the two oldest branches.
branches.cn: 路与货：穿越地形与买卖货物，是最老的两支。

branches.en: PAPER PASSED ON: a draft changes hands, and the verb names the passing.
branches.cn: 票据易手：汇票从一只手到另一只手，动词命名的正是这次传递。

branches.en: GAIN EXTRACTED: bargaining is also the art of pulling a concession toward oneself.
branches.cn: 争得好处：谈判也是把让步拉向自己这一边的本事。

intro.en: Negotiate is a Latin verb made of a negative particle and a noun for leisure, which is why the family can be read as a small sentence about work.
intro.cn: negotiate 是一个由否定小品词与「闲暇」之名词构成的拉丁动词，因此这个词族可以读成一句关于「工作」的小句子。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium yields negotiari, negotiator and negotiatio, and those in turn give the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 negotium 衍生 negotiari、negotiator 与 negotiatio，这些又衍生出英语的整个词族。

items.example: The particle turns leisure into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个小品词把「闲暇」变成「不得闲」。

items.example: The noun supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的后一半。

items.example: The compound began as a description of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词最初是对「工作」的描述。

items.example: The verb entered English through this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词正是经这个形式传入。

items.example: They negotiated the contract.
items.exampleCN: 他们就合同进行了谈判。

items.example: The negotiation lasted three days.
items.exampleCN: 谈判持续了三天。

items.example: The chief negotiator spoke last.
items.exampleCN: 首席谈判者最后发言。

items.meaning: able to be discussed or transferred
items.example: The salary is negotiable.
items.exampleCN: 薪资可以商量。

items.example: The lease was renegotiated last spring.
items.exampleCN: 租约去年春天重新谈过。

items.example: Renegotiation delayed the opening.
items.exampleCN: 重新谈判推迟了开业。

definition_zh: 可协商的；可转让兑现的；可通行的
definition_en: open to being discussed and changed, able to be transferred to another holder, or able to be crossed
core_image: 价签旁用铅笔写了一行小字，意思是这数字还能动
scene: 拍卖行的图录上，底价旁边有一行铅笔小字，写着「可再议」。The asking price is negotiable, so the buyer waited until the last hour to make an offer.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiable 指「条件可以再谈、不必照字面接受」（第 1 个义项：价格留有余地）；句意为要价可以商量，因此买家一直等到最后一个小时才出价。可辨识物件：图录、铅笔小字、价签、举牌。

pos.zh: （票据）可转让兑现的；（道路）可通行的

senses.title: A price left open to bargaining
senses.titleCN: 价格留有余地，可以再谈
senses.definition: of a price or fee, not fixed, so that an offer below it may be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或费用没有定死，低于标价的出价也可能被接受
senses.example: The fee is negotiable if the work is finished early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果能提前完工，费用可以商量。
senses.why: the suffix -able turns the bargaining verb into a property: what can be bargained over is negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把「讨价还价」这个动作变成一种性质：能拿去谈的，就是 negotiable。

senses.title: Terms open to adjustment
senses.titleCN: 条款可以经过商谈改动
senses.definition: of clauses in a contract, capable of being changed by discussion
senses.definitionCN: 指合同中的条款能够通过商谈修改
senses.example: Every clause is negotiable except the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 除交货日期外，每一条款都可以商量。
senses.why: a clause is negotiable when it is still on the table, and closed when the parties stop talking about it.
senses.whyCN: 条款只要还在桌上，就是可谈的；双方不再谈它，就成了定局。

senses.title: Paper that can change hands
senses.definition: of a cheque, bill or note, legally transferable to another holder
senses.definitionCN: 指支票、汇票或本票在法律上可以转给另一个持有人
senses.example: A negotiable instrument can be passed on by endorsement.
senses.exampleCN: 可流通票据能通过背书转让。
senses.why: commerce reuses the bargaining idea: a bill whose ownership can be handed over is a bill that can be dealt with.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用「可谈」的思路：所有权能交出去的票据，就是能被处置的票据。

senses.title: A dispute that can be talked out
senses.titleCN: 争端可以通过谈判解决
senses.definition: of a conflict, capable of being settled by discussion rather than by force
senses.definitionCN: 指冲突能够通过商谈而非强制手段解决
senses.example: The dispute was negotiable, so no court action followed.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争议可以谈，因此没有走到诉讼。
senses.why: calling a dispute negotiable is a judgement about method: words may still work.
senses.whyCN: 说一场争端 negotiable，其实是在判断「办法」：话还管用。

senses.title: Ground that can be crossed
senses.definition: of a route, pass or slope, possible to travel over
senses.definitionCN: 指路线、隘口或坡面能够通行
senses.example: The pass is negotiable only from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 这道隘口只有六月到九月可以通行。
senses.why: the physical branch of the verb survives here: what can be got through is literally negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 动词里那条「身体通过」的分支在此留存：能过得去的，字面上就是 negotiable。

senses.title: A person willing to bargain
senses.titleCN: 指人愿意谈、不把话堵死
senses.definition: of a person or a position, willing to discuss and give ground
senses.definitionCN: 指人或立场愿意商谈、肯作让步
senses.example: She remains negotiable on the price but not on the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她在价格上仍可谈，在期限上则不让步。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the matter to the holder: a person is negotiable when nothing is shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「事情」移到「持事的人」：人 negotiable，是说他没有把门关死。

senses.title: A draft that can be cashed
senses.definition: of a draft, able to be paid out or accepted for value at a bank
senses.definitionCN: 指汇票能在银行兑现或被承付
senses.example: Travellers may find the draft negotiable at any branch.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客会发现这张汇票在任何一家分行都能兑付。
senses.why: banks say a draft is negotiable when they will buy it, which is the transfer sense seen from the counter.
senses.whyCN: 银行说一张汇票 negotiable，意思是它愿意买下它；这是从柜台那一侧看到的「转让」义。

senses.title: A clause open to periodic review
senses.titleCN: 条款按固定周期可再议
senses.definition: of a rent or a royalty, subject to renegotiation at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 指租金或提成按约定的周期可以重新商定
senses.example: The rent is negotiable every five years.
senses.exampleCN: 租金每五年可以重新议定一次。
senses.why: a review clause keeps an agreement deliberately unfinished, so the same adjective marks it.
senses.whyCN: 复审条款故意让协议「不封口」，于是同一个形容词也用来标记它。

intro.en: Negotiable is the Latin-derived bargaining verb plus -able, the ending that marks what can be done. It entered English through commercial law. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiable 是那个源自拉丁语的「谈判」动词加上 -able 构成，后者标记「可以被做」；它经商业法进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business' was built from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure', so trade was described as the absence of free time.
items.cn: negotium「生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成，于是「买卖」被描述为「没有空闲」。

items.en: The verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business', and its participle supplied the stem used by English.
items.cn: 动词 negotiari 意为「经商」，其分词提供英语所用的词干。

items.en: The ending -abilis marked what can be done or what serves a purpose; through French it became the English -able that builds hundreds of adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -abilis 标记「可被做」或「可供使用」；经法语变为英语的 -able，构成数以百计的形容词。

items.en: The adjective appears in English commercial writing in the eighteenth century, first of bills and notes that could be transferred.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪的商业文书中出现，最初用于可以转让的汇票与本票。

items.en: From paper the word spread to prices, contracts and finally to roads and slopes that can be got through.
items.cn: 从票据出发，这个词扩展到价格、合同，最后扩展到能过得去的道路与坡面。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest commercial citation is dated differently across dictionaries, and the deeper origin of otium is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对最早的商业书证年代说法不一；otium 的更早来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words whose endings make them look like relatives of this one; group two holds adjectives with a genuinely similar reach.
note.cn: 第一组收因词尾相似而看来像本词亲属的词；第二组收意义上确实相近的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare 'to sail', built on navis 'ship' and agere 'drive': a river that ships can pass, not a price that can be argued.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare「航行」，由 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成：指可供船行的河，而非可议的价。

entries.definition: From negligere 'to disregard', built on legere 'to pick up'; it means too small to matter, with no bargaining sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 negligere「忽视」，由 legere「拾取」构成；意为小到可以忽略，与「谈判」无关。

entries.definition: The verb this adjective comes from: to bargain, or to get through a hard passage.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词所出的动词：讨价还价，或通过难走的一段。

entries.definition: The noun for the talking itself; the adjective describes a property of what that talking can change.
entries.definitionCN: 指商谈这件事本身的名词；形容词则描述「被商谈改变」的那种性质。

entries.definition: Able to be altered without breaking; broader than negotiable, which needs two parties to agree.
entries.definitionCN: 能改动而不折断；比 negotiable 宽，后者需要双方同意。

entries.definition: Able to be handed to another owner; it covers only the commercial branch of negotiable.
entries.definitionCN: 能交给另一个所有者的；只覆盖 negotiable 的商业那一支。

entries.definition: Open to dispute rather than open to a deal; a debatable point may never be settled by bargaining.
entries.definitionCN: 可以争论，而不是可以成交；可争之点未必能靠谈判定下来。

entries.definition: Liable to change without anyone deciding; negotiable implies the change would come from agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 会自行变动；而 negotiable 暗示变动来自双方同意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure' gives the business stem, and -able adds 'can be'.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」给出「生意」词干，-able 再加上「可以被」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, negotiability, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、negotiability、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split into two fields: a negotiable price, a negotiable instrument.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分成两个领域：可议的价格、可流通的票据。

normal.en: The usual negation is not a prefix but the phrase not open to negotiation.
normal.cn: 常见的否定并不是加前缀，而是「不容商量」这一说法。

normal.en: The opposite adjective non-negotiable is common in politics and in contracts.
normal.cn: 相反的形容词 non-negotiable 在政治与合同中都很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag written in pencil rather than ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用铅笔而不是墨水写的价签。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose hinge is loose enough to open a little wider.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门的铰链松得还能再开一点。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge that sways but still carries a walker across.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会晃、却仍能把人送过对岸的索桥。

examples.en: The salary is negotiable, but the start date is not.
examples.cn: 薪资可以谈，入职日期不可以。

examples.en: Only the lower path is negotiable in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天只有下面那条小路能走。

examples.en: The note is negotiable at any bank in the city.
examples.cn: 这张本票在本市任何银行都可兑付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「negotiate（谈判）+ able（能）」——能拿去谈的 → 可协商的

root: 拉丁 negotium（生意，字面「不得闲」）+ -abilis（可被……的）→ 英语 negotiable；商业法中最先指可转让票据，后扩展到价格、条款与可通行地形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: can this still be moved? A price, a clause, a bill, a dispute, a pass, a person, a draft and a rent clause can each be moved in a different way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：这东西还能不能动。价格、条款、票据、争端、隘口、人、汇票与租金条款，各自以不同方式「能动」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag written in pencil, with a small note in the margin saying it can still change.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张用铅笔写的价签，页边还有一行小字说这数字还能改。

branches.en: TALKABLE TERMS: a price and a clause stay unfinished while the parties keep talking.
branches.cn: 可谈的条款：只要双方还在谈，价格与条款就保持「未封口」。

branches.en: PAPER IN MOTION: a bill passes by endorsement, and a draft is bought at the counter.
branches.cn: 会动的纸：汇票靠背书传递，本票在柜台被买下。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CONFLICTS: a quarrel can be talked out, and a person stays open to a deal.
branches.cn: 人与争端：争执可以谈开，人也始终留着成交的余地。

branches.en: GROUND: the old physical branch, where a pass opens for a few months each year.
branches.cn: 地形：最具体的一支，隘口每年只开放几个月。

branches.en: DELIBERATE GAP: a review clause keeps the agreement open on a schedule.
branches.cn: 刻意留的缝：复审条款按周期把协议重新打开。

intro.en: Negotiable is a Latin business noun turned into an adjective by a suffix that English borrowed and never stopped using.
intro.cn: negotiable 是一个拉丁「生意」名词，靠一个英语借来后一直沿用的后缀变成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun negotium and the verb negotiari supply the stem, while -abilis supplies the meaning of possibility.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 negotium 与动词 negotiari 提供词干，-abilis 提供「可能」之意。

items.example: The particle negates leisure.
items.exampleCN: 这个小品词否定「闲暇」。

items.example: Leisure is the second element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 「闲暇」是复合词的第二部分。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种可能性。

items.meaning: able to be bargained or transferred
items.example: The price is negotiable.
items.exampleCN: 价格可以商量。

items.example: Negotiability made the note useful.
items.exampleCN: 可流通性使这张本票有用。

items.example: They negotiate every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天都谈判。

items.example: The negotiation took a week.
items.exampleCN: 谈判进行了一周。

items.example: The negotiator kept her voice low.
items.exampleCN: 谈判者把声音放得很低。

items.example: The safety rule is non-negotiable.
items.exampleCN: 这条安全规定不容商量。

items.example: They renegotiate the rent every five years.
items.exampleCN: 他们每五年重谈一次租金。

definition_zh: 协议；一致意见；同意；（语法）一致关系
definition_en: an arrangement or understanding reached between people, the act of agreeing, or the matching of forms in grammar
core_image: 两个人把各自的手放在同一张纸的同一行上
scene: 审阅室里，两份文件的同一处被画上对钩，笔迹不同，位置一样。The two sides signed an agreement that ends five years of litigation.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 指「双方商定并落到纸面的共同安排」（第 2 个义项：正式的书面协议）；句意为双方签署了一份协议，结束了持续五年的诉讼。可辨识物件：签字笔、两份文件、对钩、封蜡印。

senses.title: An understanding reached
senses.definition: a shared position that two or more parties have arrived at
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方共同走到的一个立场
senses.example: An agreement was reached after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜之后达成了共识。
senses.why: the noun names the settled state that the verb agree produces, so it can exist before anything is written.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名 agree 所产生的「已定」状态，因此它可以在写成文字之前就存在。

senses.title: A formal written contract
senses.definition: a document in which parties record binding terms
senses.definitionCN: 各方在其中记下有约束力的条款的文件
senses.example: The two sides signed an agreement that ends five years of litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了一份协议，结束了持续五年的诉讼。
senses.why: once a consensus is written and signed, the word moves from the understanding to the paper that proves it.
senses.whyCN: 共识一旦写成并签字，这个词就从「理解」移到「证明这份理解的纸」。

senses.title: The act of agreeing
senses.definition: the action of giving consent or expressing assent
senses.definitionCN: 给出同意或表达赞同的行为
senses.example: His agreement came as a surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他的同意出乎意料。
senses.why: English allows the noun of an act to stand for the act itself, so agreement can be a single nod.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许行为名词指行为本身，因此一个点头也可以叫 agreement。

senses.title: Harmony between people
senses.titleCN: 人与人之间的和睦无争
senses.definition: a state in which people live or work without quarrelling
senses.definitionCN: 人们一起生活或工作而不争吵的状态
senses.example: The two neighbours live in agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位邻居相处和睦。
senses.why: absence of conflict is agreement viewed as a standing condition rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: 没有冲突，就是把 agreement 看作一种持续状态，而不是一次事件。

senses.title: Consistency between accounts
senses.definition: the matching of two sets of facts, figures or reports
senses.definitionCN: 两组事实、数字或报告彼此对得上
senses.example: There is agreement between the two records.
senses.exampleCN: 两份记录彼此相符。
senses.why: the same word for people who think alike was applied to things that line up, once comparison became a habit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「比较」成为习惯，原本形容人想法相同的词，就被用到彼此对得上的事物上。

senses.title: Grammar concord
senses.definition: the correspondence of a verb with its subject, or of an adjective with its noun, in number or gender
senses.definitionCN: 动词与主语、或形容词与名词在数或性上相互对应
senses.example: In English, agreement shows in the verb ending.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语里，一致关系体现在动词词尾上。
senses.why: grammar borrowed the social word for two forms that must think alike.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个社会性的词，来形容两个必须「想法一致」的形式。

senses.title: Consent or approval
senses.definition: official permission given by a person or body
senses.definitionCN: 由某个人或机构给出的正式许可
senses.example: The plan needs the committee's agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案需要委员会的同意。
senses.why: in committees, agreeing is the act that unlocks action, so the noun comes to mean the permission itself.
senses.whyCN: 在委员会里，「同意」正是解锁行动的那一步，于是这个名词也指许可本身。

senses.title: A private unwritten arrangement
senses.definition: an arrangement kept between parties without a formal document
senses.definitionCN: 各方之间不作正式文件而保有的安排
senses.example: They had a private agreement about the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们关于那座花园有一个私下的约定。
senses.why: the word does not require paper, so it covers the handshake that everyone remembers and nobody writes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词并不要求纸面，因此也涵盖那种人人记得、却无人写下的握手之约。

intro.en: Agreement came into English from Old French agreement, the noun of agreer 'to please, consent', whose root is Latin gratus 'pleasing, thankful'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: agreement 经古法语 agreement 进入英语，它是动词 agreer「使满意、同意」的名词，词根为拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的、感激的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome, thankful'. Its deeper origin is not settled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstructed form rather than an attested word.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、心怀感激的」。其更深来源没有定论；为它提出的印欧形式都是重构形式，而非有书证的词。

items.en: The phrase a gre, 'at pleasure', from Latin gratum, produced agreer: to please someone, to be to someone's liking.
items.cn: 由拉丁 gratum 而来的短语 a gre「合意、如意」，构成了 agreer：使某人满意，合某人心意。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to please or satisfy', and the noun agreement appears in the same period meaning consent.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，义为「使满意、使满足」；名词 agreement 同期出现，意为「同意」。

items.en: The modern sense 'be of one mind' develops in the middle of the fifteenth century, when the verb stops meaning only 'please'.
items.cn: 「想法相同」的现代义在十五世纪中叶发展出来，此时动词不再只表示「使满意」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century a written, signed agreement had become the ordinary instrument of commerce and property, and the paper sense took over.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，写成并签署的 agreement 已成为商业与财产事务的常用文书，指纸面的义项因而占了上风。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): dictionaries date the noun's first appearance differently by a decade, and the pre-Latin history of gratus remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对这个名词首见的年代相差可达十年；gratus 在拉丁语之前的来历仍是重构。

note.en: Group one holds words close in shape but built on other roots; group two holds nouns for settled arrangements, each with a different degree of formality.
note.cn: 第一组收形近而词根不同的词；第二组收表示「议定之事」的名词，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin aggregare, built on grex 'flock': to gather into a whole, with no root shared with agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aggregare，由 grex「群」构成：聚合成一个整体，与 agreement 不共词根。

entries.definition: Also built on grex 'flock': to come together in a crowd, a gathering of bodies rather than of opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 grex「群」构成：聚成一群，是身体的聚集，而非意见的汇合。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same family: pleasant, or willing to consent.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的形容词：令人愉快的，或愿意同意的。

entries.definition: The same noun with a negative prefix: the state or an instance of not agreeing.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀的同名词：不同意这一状态或一次不同意。

entries.definition: A written instrument enforceable in law; an agreement may be informal and still be called one.
entries.definitionCN: 可在法律上强制执行的书面文书；而 agreement 可以是非正式的。

entries.definition: A shared view that may rest on goodwill rather than on terms; it is the least formal of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 可能靠善意而非条款维持的共同看法；是本组中最不正式的一个。

entries.definition: General agreement across a group, especially after discussion; it stresses breadth rather than binding terms.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人之间、尤其经讨论后的普遍一致；侧重「广」，而非「有约束力」。

entries.definition: A formal settlement between states or bodies; it carries more ceremony than agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 国家或机构之间的正式协定；比 agreement 更有仪式感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is agree plus -ment, the ending that turns an act into a thing.
normal.cn: 这个名词是 agree 加 -ment，后者把一个行为变成一件东西。

normal.en: The family runs agree, agreement, agreeable, agreed, disagree, disagreement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 agree、agreement、agreeable、agreed、disagree、disagreement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: reach an agreement, sign an agreement, honour an agreement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各个阶段：达成协议、签署协议、遵守协议。

normal.en: The grammatical sense appears in the phrase subject-verb agreement.
normal.cn: 语法义出现在「主谓一致」这一说法里。

normal.en: The opposite noun takes the prefix dis- and keeps the same ending.
normal.cn: 相反的名词加上 dis- 前缀，词尾不变。

abstract.en: Picture two hands on the same line of a page, one above the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手落在同一页的同一行上，一只在另一只上方。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks set to the same minute though wound at different times.
abstract.cn: 想象两只钟在不同时间上弦，却指在同一分钟。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from both banks and meeting exactly in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥从两岸同时修起，正好在中间接上。

examples.en: The agreement was never put in writing, yet both families kept it.
examples.cn: 这份约定从未写成文字，两家人却都遵守。

examples.en: There is broad agreement among historians about the cause of the famine.
examples.cn: 历史学家对这场饥荒的成因有广泛共识。

examples.en: The verb's agreement with its subject is easy to hear in speech.
examples.cn: 动词与主语的一致关系在口语里很容易听出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（一个）+ gree（合意）+ ment（名词）」——合成一个大家都点头的东西 → 协议

root: 古法语 agreement 出自 agreer「使满意、同意」，源头为拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」；英语中先有「满意」义，十五世纪中叶才固定「意见相同」，后衍生书面协议义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the inner state to the paper: first a shared view, then the signing, then the act, the calm, the matching of facts, the grammar rule, the permission, and finally the handshake nobody wrote down.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从心里走到纸上：先是共同看法，再是签字，然后是行为、和睦、事实相符、语法规则、许可，最后是无人写下的握手之约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands resting on the same line of one page.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手落在同一页的同一行上。

branches.en: WHAT WAS UNDERSTOOD: a consensus may live in memory alone, or be written and signed.
branches.cn: 彼此理解了什么：共识可以只活在记忆里，也可以写成文字并签字。

branches.en: PAPER AND PERMISSION: the signed page authorizes, and a committee's assent unlocks the plan.
branches.cn: 纸面与许可：签下的那一页授权，而委员会的同意为方案开锁。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE STATE: one nod, and a long peace between neighbours.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：一个点头，以及邻里之间长久的和睦。

branches.en: FACTS THAT LINE UP: two records agree when their entries correspond.
branches.cn: 对得上的事实：两份记录条目相应，便算相符。

branches.en: FORMS THAT LINE UP: grammar applies the social word to verb and subject.
branches.cn: 对得上的形式：语法把这个社会性的词用到动词与主语身上。

intro.en: Agreement is a French noun ending that English added to a French verb; both pieces are still productive in English today.
intro.cn: agreement 是英语加在法语动词上的法语名词词尾，两部分在今天仍能造新词。

latinIntro.en: The root gratus 'pleasing' also yields gratitude and grateful, while the noun ending -ment marks result or action.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 gratus「令人愉快的」还衍生出 gratitude 与 grateful，名词词尾 -ment 表示结果或行为。

items.meaningCN: 令人愉快的；心怀感激的
items.example: The root supplies the sense of something welcome.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「受欢迎」的意思。

items.example: The phrase underlies the French verb of consent.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是法语「同意」动词的底子。

items.example: The French verb crossed into English in the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词在十四世纪进入英语。

items.meaning: to consent, to be of one mind
items.example: They agreed on the price.
items.exampleCN: 他们就价格达成一致。

items.exampleCN: 协议在中午签署。

items.example: The terms were agreeable to both.
items.exampleCN: 这些条件双方都乐意接受。

items.example: The evening passed agreeably.
items.exampleCN: 那个晚上过得很愉快。

items.example: They met at the agreed hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们在约定的时间见面。

items.example: The disagreement was never resolved.
items.exampleCN: 那处分歧始终没有解决。

items.example: She wrote in gratitude for the help.
items.exampleCN: 她写信感谢那份帮助。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 令人愉快的；受欢迎的；感激的

latinEntries.meaning: a thing that pleases, a thanks

definition_zh: 同意；赞同；达成一致；相符；（食物）适宜
definition_en: to hold the same opinion, to consent, to reach an understanding, or to correspond with something else
core_image: 两双手在同一行字上停住，各自点了一下头
scene: 会开到一半，两方代表各自在纸上同一处画了对钩。Both committees agree that the bridge must be repaired before winter.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 指「两方持有相同判断」（第 1 个义项：意见一致）；句意为两个委员会都认为这座桥必须在入冬前修好。可辨识物件：对钩、两份议事日程、铅笔、窗外的桥。

collocations.zh: 承认彼此看法不同而不再争

senses.title: Hold the same opinion
senses.definition: to share a view with another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人或群体持有相同的看法
senses.example: Both committees agree that the bridge must be repaired before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 两个委员会都认为这座桥必须在入冬前修好。
senses.why: the oldest sense after 'please' was 'be of one mind', which is the core of the modern verb.
senses.whyCN: 在「使满意」之后最老的一义就是「想法相同」，这正是现代动词的核心。

senses.title: Give consent
senses.definition: to say yes to a request, plan or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 对请求、计划或提议说「可以」
senses.example: The landlord agreed to a six-month extension.
senses.exampleCN: 房东答应延期六个月。
senses.why: sharing a view and granting a request are two sides of one movement: the second person stops resisting.
senses.whyCN: 看法相同与答应请求是同一动作的两面：第二个人不再抗拒。

senses.title: Settle a matter together
senses.definition: to reach a decision or a set of terms with others
senses.definitionCN: 与别人一起作出决定或定下条件
senses.example: They agreed on a price before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在中午之前谈定了价格。
senses.why: when two parties each hold a view, agreement produces a third thing: a settled arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 两方各持一个看法，一旦相合便生出第三样东西：定下来的安排。

senses.title: Correspond with the facts
senses.titleCN: 与事实或另一说法相符
senses.definition: of accounts, figures or stories, to match one another
senses.definitionCN: 指叙述、数字或说法彼此对得上
senses.example: The witness accounts agree on every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 几位证人的叙述在每个细节上都相互吻合。
senses.why: people who think alike are said to agree, and things that line up are described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 想法相同的人被说成 agree，彼此对得上的事物也就用了同一个词。

senses.title: Match in grammar
senses.definition: of a word, to correspond with another in number, gender or person
senses.definitionCN: 指一个词在数、性或人称上与另一个词相应
senses.example: The verb agrees with its subject in number.
senses.exampleCN: 动词在数上与主语保持一致。
senses.why: grammar treats two forms as parties that must hold the same view, and borrows the social verb.
senses.whyCN: 语法把两个形式当成必须「同意见」的两方，于是借用了这个社会性的动词。

senses.title: Suit a person's constitution
senses.definition: of food, climate or a remedy, to have a good effect on someone
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、气候或疗法对某人有良好作用
senses.example: Rich food does not agree with him.
senses.exampleCN: 油腻的食物他吃了不舒服。
senses.why: the body and the thing taken into it are pictured as two parties that either get on or do not.
senses.whyCN: 身体与吃进去的东西被想象成两方，要么合得来，要么合不来。

senses.title: End a quarrel
senses.definition: to stop quarrelling and come to terms after a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在争执之后停止争吵并达成一致
senses.example: The brothers agreed after the lawyer intervened.
senses.exampleCN: 律师介入之后，兄弟俩达成了和解。
senses.why: the result of agreeing is also the end of disagreement, so the verb covers the whole repair of a broken relation.
senses.whyCN: 同意带来的结果也正是不同意的结束，因此这个动词涵盖一段破裂关系的整个修复。

senses.title: Fix terms in advance
senses.definition: to arrange a price, a date or terms by negotiation, used with a direct object
senses.definitionCN: 经商谈把价格、日期或条件定下来，带直接宾语
senses.example: The union agreed a new pay scale.
senses.exampleCN: 工会谈定了新的工资等级。
senses.why: British usage allows a direct object here, so the verb can mean 'settle' rather than only 'share a view'.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法允许它带直接宾语，于是这个动词可以表示「把条件定下来」，而不只是「看法相同」。

intro.en: Agree came from Old French agreer, from the phrase a gre 'at pleasure', whose gre goes back to Latin gratum, from gratus 'pleasing'. The sense 'be of one mind' is fifteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: agree 来自古法语 agreer，出自短语 a gre「合意、如意」，其中的 gre 上溯拉丁 gratum，源自 gratus「令人愉快的」。「意见相同」这一义是十五世纪的产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome, thankful'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established; every deeper form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、心怀感激的」。它在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论；为它引用的更深形式均属重构。

items.en: The phrase a gre, 'according to pleasure', is built on gre, from Latin gratum, and it described what was done to someone's liking.
items.cn: 短语 a gre「依心意而行」由 gre 构成，gre 出自拉丁 gratum，用来描述「合某人心意」的做法。

items.en: Agreer meant 'to please, to satisfy, to be acceptable', and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century with those senses first.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使满意、使满足、可被接受」，英语在十四世纪借入时最先用的正是这些义项。

items.en: The sense 'to be of one mind' appears in the middle of the fifteenth century, and it gradually displaced the older 'please' reading.
items.cn: 「意见相同」这一义在十五世纪中叶出现，并逐步取代较早的「使满意」读法。

items.en: Later English extended the verb to matching accounts, to grammatical concord, to food that suits the body, and to settling terms in advance.
items.cn: 后来的英语把这个动词扩展到彼此相符的叙述、语法一致、合身体的食物，以及预先议定条件。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): dictionaries date the 'one mind' sense differently, and the deeper etymology of gratus cannot be settled from the attested words.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对「意见相同」义的年代说法不一；gratus 更早的词源无法仅凭有书证的词确定。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble agree in spelling but belong to other roots; group two holds verbs of assent with different degrees of force.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写上像 agree、却属于别的词根的词；第二组收表示「赞同」的动词，力道各不相同。

entries.definition: From Old French agrever, from Latin gravare 'to weigh down', built on gravis 'heavy'; it means to wrong or distress someone.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 agrever、拉丁 gravare「压重」，由 gravis「重的」构成；意为使受冤屈、使苦恼。

entries.definition: Built on Latin grex 'flock': to collect into one total, a gathering of units rather than of opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 grex「群」构成：汇成一个总数，是单位的集合，而非意见的汇合。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: settled by consent, as in the agreed price.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词：经同意而定下的，如「议定的价格」。

entries.definition: The adjective of the family: pleasant to be with, or willing to consent.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的形容词：相处愉快，或愿意同意。

entries.definition: To give permission for something done by another; it looks at the granting side, not at a shared view.
entries.definitionCN: 准许别人去做某事；看的是「准许」这一面，而非「共同看法」。

entries.definition: A formal verb for holding the same opinion, common in judgements and minutes.
entries.definitionCN: 表示持相同意见的正式动词，常见于判决书与会议记录。

entries.definition: To express agreement to a proposal, usually formally and after consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 对提议表示同意，通常正式且经过考虑。

entries.definition: To agree to a demand, often reluctantly; it stresses giving way rather than meeting halfway.
entries.definitionCN: 同意某项要求，常含勉强；侧重「让」，而非「折中」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'pleasing', so agreeing was first finding something acceptable.
normal.cn: 词根意为「令人愉快的」，因此「同意」最初是「觉得可以接受」。

normal.en: The family runs agree, agreement, agreeable, agreed, disagree, disagreement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 agree、agreement、agreeable、agreed、disagree、disagreement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases divide the prepositions: agree with a person, agree to a plan, agree on a price.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出介词：同意某人用 with，同意计划用 to，就价格一致用 on。

normal.en: The grammar sense is always subject and verb: the verb agrees with its subject.
normal.cn: 语法义总是主语与动词：动词与主语保持一致。

normal.en: The food sense is negative in practice: something does not agree with you.
normal.cn: 食物义在实际用法里多是否定的：某样东西你吃了不舒服。

abstract.en: Picture two people nodding at the same instant without looking at each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人没有看对方，却在同一瞬间点头。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers laid side by side and their marks lining up exactly.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并排放着，刻度正好对齐。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake that lasts a second longer than usual.
abstract.cn: 想象一次比平常多停了一秒的握手。

examples.en: They agree about the cause but not about the remedy.
examples.cn: 他们对成因看法一致，对解决办法却不一致。

examples.en: He agreed to lend the van for the weekend.
examples.cn: 他答应周末把面包车借出来。

examples.en: Spicy food never agreed with her stomach.
examples.cn: 辛辣食物一向不合她的胃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（一个）+ gree（合意）」——合成一个意思 → 同意

root: 古法语 agreer「使满意、同意」，出自短语 a gre「合意」，源头为拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」；「意见相同」义十五世纪中叶成型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hinge: two parties stop differing. The hinge is then applied to requests, prices, facts, grammar, food, quarrels and terms fixed in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项绕同一个铰链转：两方不再相异。这个铰链随后被用于请求、价格、事实、语法、食物、争执以及预先定下的条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands stopping on the same line of a page, each giving a small nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手停在同一页的同一行上，各自轻轻一点头。

branches.en: TWO MINDS ALIKE: a shared opinion, and the same word applied to accounts that correspond.
branches.cn: 两心相同：先是共同看法，同一个词再用到彼此相符的叙述上。

branches.en: FROM YES TO TERMS: consent to a request hardens into a settled price or date.
branches.cn: 从答应到条款：对请求的应允，凝成定下的价格或日期。

branches.en: FORMS THAT MUST THINK ALIKE: grammar borrows the social hinge for subject and verb.
branches.cn: 必须同意见的形式：语法为主语与动词借来这个社会性的铰链。

branches.en: THE BODY'S VERDICT: food either gets on with the body or does not.
branches.cn: 身体的裁决：食物要么与身体合得来，要么合不来。

branches.en: REPAIR AND FORESIGHT: the hinge closes a quarrel, or locks terms before trouble starts.
branches.cn: 修复与预谋：这个铰链或把争执合上，或在麻烦发生前把条件锁好。

intro.en: Agree is a French verb in English clothing, and the pieces that built it still appear in English words about pleasure and consent.
intro.cn: agree 是一个穿上英语外衣的法语动词，构成它的部件仍出现在表示「愉快」与「同意」的英语词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus 'pleasing' gives agree, gratitude, grateful and grace, while the French phrase a gre supplies the shape of the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」衍生 agree、gratitude、grateful 与 grace，而法语短语 a gre 提供动词的外形。

items.exampleCN: 词根带着「受欢迎」的意思。

items.example: The noun survives inside the French phrase of consent.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词留在表示同意的法语短语里。

items.example: The French verb was borrowed whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词被整体借入。

items.example: They agree on the main point.
items.exampleCN: 他们在要点上看法一致。

items.example: The agreement was signed.
items.exampleCN: 协议已经签署。

items.example: The terms were agreeable.
items.exampleCN: 条件是可以接受的。

items.example: They parted agreeably.
items.exampleCN: 他们愉快地告别。

items.example: The two experts disagree.
items.exampleCN: 两位专家意见不同。

items.example: The disagreement lasted a year.
items.exampleCN: 分歧持续了一年。
