definition_en: a difference of opinion, a quarrel, or a failure of two things to correspond
core_image: 两份记录上，同一行被两支笔划向相反的方向
scene: 同一份调查记录摊在桌上，两个人的笔在两处做了方向相反的标记。There was open disagreement between the survey team and the ministry over the cause of the drop.
sceneCN: 这里 disagreement 指「两方对同一件事的判断不一致」（第 1 个义项：意见分歧）；句意为调查组与部里对下降的成因存在公开分歧。可辨识物件：摊开的记录、两支笔、相反方向的标记、茶杯。

pos.zh: 异议（正式提出的不同意见）

senses.title: A difference of opinion
senses.definition: a situation in which two people or groups hold different views
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或两方持有不同看法的情形
senses.example: There was open disagreement between the survey team and the ministry over the cause of the drop.
senses.exampleCN: 调查组与部里对下降的成因存在公开分歧。
senses.why: the noun is agreement with the prefix of separation: where agreement joins, disagreement keeps two positions apart.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是加了「分开」前缀的 agreement：agreement 把两方接合，disagreement 让两个立场保持距离。

senses.title: A quarrel out loud
senses.definition: an instance of arguing, often heated and personal
senses.definitionCN: 一次争吵，常带火气与人身针对
senses.example: A loud disagreement ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一场大声的争执结束了会议。
senses.why: a difference of view becomes an event when voices rise, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 当声音抬高，看法上的不同就变成一桩事件，英语用同一个名词指称两者。

senses.title: The act of not agreeing
senses.definition: the action of refusing to assent or of stating opposition
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝同意或表明反对的行为
senses.example: His disagreement was recorded in the minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的不同意被记进了会议记录。
senses.why: naming the act lets the record show who did not nod, even when the motion passed.
senses.whyCN: 为这个行为命名，记录里才能看出谁没有点头，即使动议已经通过。

senses.title: Two accounts that do not match
senses.titleCN: 两种说法或数据对不上
senses.definition: an inconsistency between two sets of facts, figures or reports
senses.definitionCN: 两组事实、数字或报告之间存在的矛盾
senses.example: The disagreement between the two lists was easy to spot.
senses.exampleCN: 两份清单之间的出入一眼就能看出。
senses.why: things that cannot agree are described with the word used for people who cannot, so the noun covers mismatches.
senses.whyCN: 对不上的事物，被用来说「人合不来」的那个词来描述，于是这个名词也涵盖不对应。

senses.title: A dispute taken to a tribunal
senses.definition: a formal conflict between parties that is brought to arbitration or court
senses.definitionCN: 当事人之间被提交仲裁或法院的正式冲突
senses.example: The disagreement went to arbitration.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争议被提交仲裁。
senses.why: law needs a neutral word for a conflict it must handle, and disagreement serves without assigning blame.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个中性的词来指称它必须处理的冲突，disagreement 不带归罪色彩，正好合用。

senses.title: Recorded dissent
senses.titleCN: 对裁决正式提出的异议
senses.definition: a formal statement of opposition by a member of a body
senses.definitionCN: 某一机构的成员正式提出的反对陈述
senses.example: Two members filed a disagreement with the ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 两名成员对裁决提出了异议。
senses.why: institutions file what they cannot shout, so the quarrel sense is cooled into a document.
senses.whyCN: 机构不能喊，只能归档，于是「争执」这一义被冷却成一份文书。

senses.title: A lasting split between schools
senses.titleCN: 学派或党派之间的长期分裂
senses.definition: a prolonged division of opinion between groups that hold rival positions
senses.definitionCN: 持对立立场的群体之间长期的意见分裂
senses.example: The disagreement between the two schools lasted a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 两个学派之间的分歧持续了一代人。
senses.why: when a difference of view hardens into tradition, the noun describes a standing line rather than an episode.
senses.whyCN: 当看法上的不同固化为传统，这个名词描述的就是一条长期的分界线，而不是一次事件。

senses.title: Refusal to accept a claim
senses.definition: a reasoned refusal to accept a theory, a finding or a premise
senses.definitionCN: 有理由地拒绝接受某个理论、结论或前提
senses.example: Her disagreement with the standard model was published in full.
senses.exampleCN: 她反对标准模型的意见被完整发表。
senses.why: this sense is intellectual rather than personal: the object is a claim, not a colleague.
senses.whyCN: 这一义是智识上的而非人际上的：所指的是一个主张，而不是某位同事。

intro.en: Disagreement is the negative prefix dis- added to agreement, whose root is Latin gratus 'pleasing'. The prefix means apart or in different directions. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: disagreement 是表「分开」的否定前缀 dis- 加在 agreement 上构成，后者的词根是拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」。这个前缀意为「分开、朝不同方向」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dis- marked separation, division or reversal. Attached to a word of joining, it produced the exact opposite without any new root.
items.cn: dis- 标记分离、分裂或反转。把它加在表示「接合」的词上，不必另造词根就得到相反的意思。

items.en: Gratus 'pleasing, welcome' supplied the stem of agreement through Old French; its deeper origin is unsettled and offered only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: gratus「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」经古法语提供 agreement 的词干；其更深来源没有定论，只能以重构形式提出。

items.en: The French verb agreer 'to please, consent' gave English agree and, with the noun ending, agreement.
items.cn: 法语动词 agreer「使满意、同意」给出英语的 agree，加上名词词尾即成 agreement。

items.en: The negative noun appears in the early modern period, first for a difference of opinion and later for a quarrel.
items.cn: 这个否定名词在近代早期出现，先指意见上的不同，后指争吵。

items.en: Courts and committees later adopted it for disputes and recorded dissent, where a neutral label is needed.
items.cn: 法院与委员会后来把它用于争议与记录在案的异议，因为这种场合需要一个中性的标签。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest dated example varies across dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of gratus can only be reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典给出的最早年代并不一致；gratus 在拉丁语之前的历史只能重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same negative prefix but on unrelated roots; group two holds nouns for conflict, each pitched at a different temperature.
note.cn: 第一组收同用否定前缀、词根却不相干的词；第二组收表示冲突的名词，「温度」各有不同。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to hold a different view, to quarrel, or to fail to match.
entries.definitionCN: 本名词所出的动词：持不同看法、争吵，或对不上。

entries.definition: The adjective of the family, but it describes an unpleasant person or thing, not a conflict of views.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的形容词，但它描述令人不快的人或事，而非意见冲突。

entries.definition: From Latin disparare 'to separate', built on parare 'to prepare'; it means unlike in kind, not at odds in opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 disparare「分开」，由 parare「准备」构成；意为种类上不同，而非意见相左。

entries.definition: From Old French desparagier, to marry unequally, later to belittle; it looks like this family but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 desparagier「门第不等地婚配」，后转指贬低；形似本族，却不同根。

entries.definition: A conflict argued in public or in law; it is more formal and more adversarial than a disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 公开或以法律方式争辩的冲突；比 disagreement 更正式，也更对立。

entries.definition: Disagreement that splits a group from within, from Latin dissentire 'to feel differently'.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个团体内部产生分裂的分歧，来自拉丁 dissentire「感觉不同」。

entries.definition: Irritation between people that may have no stated subject; it names the mood rather than the difference.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间的摩擦不快，未必有明确议题；命名的是气氛，而非分歧本身。

entries.definition: An open clash of interests or forces; disagreement can be quiet, whereas conflict is usually active.
entries.definitionCN: 利益或力量的公开冲撞；disagreement 可以很安静，conflict 通常已动起来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dis- 'apart' plus agreement: what should have joined is kept apart.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」加 agreement：本该接合的，被留在两边。

normal.en: The family runs disagree, disagreement, agreement, disagreeable, agree.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 disagree、disagreement、agreement、disagreeable、agree。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with a subject: a disagreement over the cause, a disagreement about the budget.
normal.cn: 固定搭配常带议题：关于成因的分歧、关于预算的分歧。

normal.en: Institutions resolve, file or record disagreements; the verb beside it is disagree.
normal.cn: 机构会化解、提交或记录分歧；与之相配的动词是 disagree。

normal.en: The opposite noun adds no prefix at all: it is simply agreement.
normal.cn: 相反的名词根本不加前缀：它就是 agreement。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows drawn on one line, pointing opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线上画着两支箭头，方向相反。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same coast with the headland drawn in different places.
abstract.cn: 想象同一段海岸的两张地图，岬角画在不同的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a table with two chairs pulled apart by a hand's width.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子旁的两把椅子被拉开一掌宽。

examples.en: A small disagreement about the schedule grew into a serious dispute.
examples.cn: 关于日程的一点小分歧，后来变成了严重的争议。

examples.en: The disagreement between the two measurements pointed to a worn instrument.
examples.cn: 两次测量之间的出入说明仪器已经磨损。

examples.en: She voiced her disagreement without naming anyone.
examples.cn: 她表达了不同意见，却没有点任何人的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（不）+ agreement（一致）」——不合成一个意思 → 分歧

root: dis-（分开、相反）+ agreement（一致，源自拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」）；把表示「接合」的词加上「分开」前缀，即得「分歧、争执」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from a quiet difference of view to a filed objection, and then to the same word used for figures that cannot be made to match.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从安静的看法不同，到正式归档的异议，再到同一个词被用于怎么也对不上的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pens marking one line in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支笔在同一行上划出相反的方向。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AS A STATE: a single difference of view, and the same difference hardened into a lasting split.
branches.cn: 作为状态的分歧：一次看法不同，以及这种不同固化为长期分裂。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AS AN EVENT: it becomes a quarrel, and the refusal itself gets recorded.
branches.cn: 作为事件的分歧：它变成一场争执，而拒绝本身被记录下来。

branches.en: FACTS APART: two lists or readings fail to correspond.
branches.cn: 事实对不上：两份清单或两次读数不能相应。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL FORM: a dispute goes to arbitration, and a member files a dissent.
branches.cn: 制度形态：争议送交仲裁，成员提交异议。

branches.en: A CLAIM REFUSED: the object is a theory rather than a person.
branches.cn: 被拒的主张：所针对的是一个理论，而不是一个人。

intro.en: Disagreement combines a Latin prefix of separation with a French noun of consent, so its two halves can be read separately.
intro.cn: disagreement 把一个拉丁「分离」前缀与一个法语「同意」名词合在一起，两半都可以单独读。

latinIntro.en: Latin dis- supplies the negative force, and gratus supplies the stem that also appears in agree, agreeable and grateful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dis- 提供否定力量，gratus 提供词干，后者也出现在 agree、agreeable 与 grateful 中。

items.example: The prefix turns joining into separation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「接合」变成「分开」。

items.example: The root supplies the consent stem.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「同意」的词干。

items.example: The two sides agree on the main point.
items.exampleCN: 两方在要点上一致。

items.example: The agreement took a year to draft.
items.exampleCN: 这份协议起草了一年。

items.example: The reviewers disagree on the cause.
items.exampleCN: 评审人对成因看法不同。

items.example: The disagreement split the committee.
items.exampleCN: 这场分歧使委员会分裂。

items.example: The room had a disagreeable smell.
items.exampleCN: 这间屋里有股难闻的气味。

items.example: He answered disagreeably.
items.exampleCN: 他答得很不客气。

items.example: They met at the agreed time.
items.exampleCN: 他们在约定时间见面。

definition_zh: 不同意；有分歧；不一致；（食物、气候）不适合
definition_en: to hold a different opinion, to quarrel, to fail to correspond, or to have a bad effect on someone
core_image: 同一张桌边，两个人把同一只杯子推向相反的方向
scene: 评审室里，两份报告对同一现象给出了两种解释。The two reviewers disagree about whether the decline is caused by climate or by hunting.
sceneCN: 这里 disagree 指「对同一件事给出不同判断」（第 1 个义项：持不同意见）；句意为两位评审人对数量下降是由气候还是由捕猎造成，意见不一致。可辨识物件：两份报告、红蓝铅笔、放大镜、窗外的林地。

pos.zh: 持不同意见；争执；不一致
（食物、气候）对某人有不良影响

senses.title: Hold a different opinion
senses.definition: to have a view that differs from another person's
senses.definitionCN: 持有与另一人不同的看法
senses.example: The two reviewers disagree about whether the decline is caused by climate or by hunting.
senses.exampleCN: 两位评审人对下降是由气候还是由捕猎造成，意见不一致。
senses.why: the prefix simply reverses agreement, so the verb means the two minds stay apart.
senses.whyCN: 前缀把 agreement 整个反过来，因此这个动词意为「两个头脑仍分开」。

senses.title: Quarrel openly
senses.definition: to argue with someone in an unfriendly way
senses.definitionCN: 以不友善的方式与人争辩
senses.example: They disagreed loudly and then stopped speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们大声吵了一场，然后不再说话。
senses.why: when the difference is voiced with heat, the same verb names the quarrel and not only the view.
senses.whyCN: 当不同被带着火气说出来，同一个动词指的就是争吵，而不只是看法。

senses.title: Fail to match
senses.titleCN: 数字或读数彼此对不上
senses.definition: of two sets of figures or measurements, not to correspond with each other
senses.definitionCN: 指两组数字或测量彼此不能对应
senses.example: The two readings disagree by three degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 两次读数相差三度。
senses.why: things are said to disagree when their accounts cannot be brought into line, just as people cannot.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西的说法无法对齐时，也说它们 disagree，正如人合不到一起。

senses.title: Sit badly with the body
senses.definition: of food, weather or a medicine, to have an unpleasant physical effect
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、天气或药物对身体产生不良作用
senses.example: Cold damp weather disagrees with her.
senses.exampleCN: 湿冷的天气让她身体不舒服。
senses.why: the body and the thing outside it are two parties that either get on or do not, and the verb keeps that frame.
senses.whyCN: 身体与体外之物是两方，要么合得来，要么合不来；这个动词沿用了这个框架。

senses.title: Refuse to approve
senses.definition: of a body or an authority, to withhold approval from a plan
senses.definitionCN: 指机构或主管对某项计划不予认可
senses.example: The board disagreed with the merger plan.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会对合并方案表示不认可。
senses.why: institutional refusal is the formal face of a difference of view, so the same verb covers a vote.
senses.whyCN: 机构的拒绝，是「看法不同」的正式面孔，因此同一个动词也能指表决。

senses.title: Differ only on details
senses.titleCN: 在大方向上一致，只在细节上不同
senses.definition: to be at variance over particulars while accepting the main point
senses.definitionCN: 接受要点，只在具体细节上与对方不同
senses.example: They disagree only on the timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只在时间安排上有分歧。
senses.why: disagreement can be partial, and the verb with a limiting phrase marks exactly where the split begins.
senses.whyCN: 分歧可以是局部的，动词加上限定短语，正好标出分裂从哪里开始。

senses.title: Contradict a record or claim
senses.titleCN: 与某份记录或主张相抵触
senses.definition: of evidence or a statement, to conflict with another account
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或陈述与另一份说法相冲突
senses.example: The new evidence disagrees with the earlier report.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据与早先的报告相抵触。
senses.why: here one account actively pushes against another, which is the mismatch sense turned adversarial.
senses.whyCN: 这里一份说法主动顶住另一份，是「对不上」这一义转为对抗性的用法。

senses.title: Dissent in writing
senses.definition: to record formal opposition to a decision of a body
senses.definitionCN: 就某一机构的决定留下正式的反对记录
senses.example: Two members disagreed with the finding in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 两名成员以书面形式对结论提出异议。
senses.why: committees turn a spoken difference into a minute, so the verb appears in the passive voice of record-keeping.
senses.whyCN: 委员会把口头上的不同变成会议记录，于是这个动词出现在「留档」的被动语态里。

intro.en: Disagree is dis- 'apart' plus agree, which came from Old French agreer and ultimately Latin gratus 'pleasing'. The verb reverses the older verb of consent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: disagree 是 dis-「分开」加 agree 构成；agree 来自古法语 agreer，最终源头为拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」。这个动词把较早的「同意」整个反过来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dis- meant apart or in opposite directions. Added to a verb of joining, it produced the exact negative without a new stem.
items.cn: dis- 意为「分开」或「朝相反方向」。加在表示「接合」的动词上，不必另造词干就得到确切的否定。

items.en: Gratus 'pleasing, welcome' is the root behind agree; its pre-Latin history is unsettled and any form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gratus「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」是 agree 背后的词根；它在拉丁语之前的历史没有定论，为它引用的形式都属重构。

items.en: Agreer 'to please, to consent' passed into English in the fourteenth century, and the negative form followed.
items.cn: agreer「使满意、同意」在十四世纪进入英语，否定形式随后出现。

items.en: Once agree had settled into the sense 'be of one mind', the negative verb could be formed by prefix alone, and it appears in the same century.
items.cn: 一旦 agree 固定为「想法相同」，否定动词就能只靠加前缀构成，它也在同一世纪出现。

items.en: Later English extended the negative verb to figures that do not correspond, to food that upsets the body, and to written dissent.
items.cn: 后来的英语把这个否定动词扩展到对不上的数字、使身体不适的食物，以及书面异议。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): dictionaries differ on the earliest dated example of the negative verb, and the deeper origin of gratus can only be reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对否定动词的最早年代说法不一；gratus 更深处的来历只能重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like disagree but belong elsewhere; group two holds verbs of opposition that differ in heat and in formality.
note.cn: 第一组收看来像 disagree、却属于别处的词；第二组收表示反对的动词，火气与正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin aggravare, built on gravis 'heavy': to make worse or to annoy, with no link to consent.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aggravare，由 gravis「重的」构成；意为使恶化或使恼火，与「同意」无关。

entries.definition: Also built on gravis 'heavy' through Old French agrever: to distress or wrong someone.
entries.definitionCN: 同样经古法语 agrever、由 gravis「重的」构成：使某人受屈或苦恼。

entries.definition: The noun of this verb: a difference of view, a quarrel, or a mismatch.
entries.definitionCN: 本动词的名词：看法不同、争执，或对不上。

entries.definition: The adjective means unpleasant, which is a different thing from holding a contrary view.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词意为令人不快，与「持相反看法」是两回事。

entries.definition: To be unlike, used of things as readily as of people; it carries no quarrel and no heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指不相同，用于事物如同用于人；不含争吵，也不带火气。

entries.definition: To declare opposition to an official decision or doctrine; it is more formal than disagree.
entries.definitionCN: 对官方决定或教义声明反对；比 disagree 正式。

entries.definition: To raise a formal objection in a meeting or a court; the objection has a procedure behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 在会议或法庭上正式提出反对；这种反对背后有程序。

entries.definition: To come into conflict sharply, of people, colours or schedules; it stresses impact rather than opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 指人、颜色或日程发生尖锐冲突；侧重「撞上」，而非「看法」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dis- reverses agree, so the verb needs no separate root of its own.
normal.cn: dis- 把 agree 反过来，因此这个动词不必另造词根。

normal.en: The family runs disagree, disagreement, agreement, disagreeable, agree.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 disagree、disagreement、agreement、disagreeable、agree。

normal.en: Prepositions divide the senses: disagree with a person, disagree about a matter, disagree on details.
normal.cn: 介词分出义项：不同意某人用 with，对某事用 about，在细节上用 on。

normal.en: The polite formula agree to disagree marks a difference that will not be settled.
normal.cn: 礼貌说法「同意各自保留意见」，标记一处不会解决的分歧。

normal.en: The food sense is almost always negative: something disagrees with you.
normal.cn: 食物义几乎总是否定的：某样东西让你不舒服。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows leaving one point in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头从同一点出发，方向相反。

abstract.en: Picture two thermometers in one room showing different readings.
abstract.cn: 想象同一间屋里的两支温度计读数不同。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pushing one door from both sides at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手同时从两侧推同一扇门。

examples.en: I disagree with the conclusion, though not with the method.
examples.cn: 我不同意这个结论，但不反对这个方法。

examples.en: The clock and the bell disagree by nearly a minute.
examples.cn: 这只钟与那口铃差了将近一分钟。

examples.en: Strong coffee disagrees with him after noon.
examples.cn: 过了中午，浓咖啡就让他不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（不）+ agree（同意）」——不点头 → 不同意

root: dis-（分开、相反）+ agree（同意，源自拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」）；由「同意」直接加否定前缀构成，无需另造词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all work by putting two things out of line: two minds, two voices, two readings, a body and its food, a board and a plan, two accounts, and a member against a ruling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都靠「把两样东西错开」起作用：两个头脑、两个声音、两次读数、身体与食物、董事会与方案、两份说法，以及成员与裁决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at one table pushing the same cup in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张桌边，两个人把同一只杯子推向相反的方向。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE OF VIEW: whole-hearted opposition, and the partial version that keeps the main point.
branches.cn: 看法不同：整体上的相反，以及保留要点的局部不同。

branches.en: FROM SHOUT TO MINUTE: a quarrel is cooled into a written objection.
branches.cn: 从喊到记：争执被冷却成书面异议。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS OUT OF LINE: two readings miss each other, and one report pushes against another.
branches.cn: 说法错开：两次读数彼此不合，一份报告顶住另一份。

branches.en: BODY AND FOOD: the old frame of two parties that must get on.
branches.cn: 身体与食物：两方必须合得来的古老框架。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL NO: a board withholds approval, which is a difference of view with a vote behind it.
branches.cn: 机构说不：董事会不予认可，即背后有表决的看法不同。

intro.en: Disagree is a prefixed French verb, and both the prefix and the root still build English words.
intro.cn: disagree 是一个加前缀的法语动词，前缀与词根至今仍在构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin dis- marks separation, and gratus 'pleasing' yields agree, agreement, agreeable and grateful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dis- 标记分离，gratus「令人愉快的」衍生 agree、agreement、agreeable 与 grateful。

items.example: The prefix reverses the verb of consent.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「同意」动词反过来。

items.example: The root supplies the consent stem.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「同意」的词干。

items.example: They agree on the price.
items.exampleCN: 他们就价格达成一致。

items.example: The reviewers disagree on the cause.
items.exampleCN: 评审人对成因看法不同。

items.example: The disagreement lasted a year.
items.exampleCN: 分歧持续了一年。

items.example: The smell was disagreeable.
items.exampleCN: 那气味令人不快。

items.example: The room was disagreeably cold.
items.exampleCN: 这间屋冷得让人难受。

items.example: The suggestion was agreeable to all.
items.exampleCN: 这个建议各方都乐意接受。

items.example: They followed the agreed plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们按照议定的方案行事。

definition_zh: 共识；共同意见；一致意见
definition_en: general agreement among a group, especially after discussion, or the view most people in a field hold
core_image: 一圈人围桌而坐，最后所有手都放在同一张纸上
scene: 表决之前，主持人再问一遍，无人再提出新的修改。After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
sceneCN: 这里 consensus 指「一群人在讨论之后形成的共同意见」（第 1 个义项：群体内的一致）；句意为辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。可辨识物件：长桌、摊开的报告、举手表决前的沉默、记录本。

senses.title: Agreement across a group
senses.titleCN: 一个群体内部的共同意见
senses.definition: a general agreement reached by the members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一群成员形成的普遍一致
senses.example: After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。
senses.why: Latin consensus simply meant 'agreement', and English kept that breadth: the noun names the state without saying how it was reached.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 consensus 本来就只表示「一致」，英语保留了这个宽度：这个名词命名状态，不说明它是怎么达成的。

senses.title: The view most people hold
senses.definition: the opinion that prevails in a field or a population at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或人群在某一时期占上风的看法
senses.example: The consensus in the field is that the warming is real.
senses.exampleCN: 该领域的主流看法是变暖确实在发生。
senses.why: when a shared view becomes the background assumption, consensus means the default position rather than a fresh agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当共同看法变成背景假设，consensus 指的就是默认立场，而不是新达成的协议。

senses.title: Agreement produced by talk
senses.titleCN: 经讨论而非表决形成的一致
senses.definition: a shared position arrived at through discussion rather than through a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨论而非正式表决得到的共同立场
senses.example: Consensus was reached without a formal ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 没有正式投票就形成了共识。
senses.why: meetings needed a word for agreement that is felt in the room before it is counted, and this noun supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 会议需要一个词，来形容那种先在会场里被感觉到、之后才被计数的同意，这个名词正好补上。

senses.title: Agreement among experts
senses.definition: the settled judgement of specialists in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域专门研究者已定下来的判断
senses.example: Scientific consensus on the age of the rock took decades to form.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这块岩石年龄的科学共识，花了几十年才形成。
senses.why: science does not vote, but it does converge, and the noun describes that convergence without implying unanimity.
senses.whyCN: 科学不作表决，却会收敛；这个名词描述这种收敛，但并不暗示全体一致。

senses.title: Sympathy among body parts
senses.titleCN: 旧医学：身体各部分的同感
senses.definition: an old physiological notion that the organs act in sympathy with one another
senses.definitionCN: 旧生理学中的观念：各器官彼此同感相应
senses.example: Early physicians wrote of a consensus among the organs.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医生写到各器官之间的同感。
senses.why: the Latin noun was borrowed first for bodily sympathy, because parts that act together were said to feel together.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最早被借用来指身体各部的同感，因为共同起作用的部位被说成「一同感受」。

senses.title: Cross-party agreement
senses.definition: a shared position adopted by rival political groups
senses.definitionCN: 对立政治团体共同采取的立场
senses.example: A consensus emerged between the parties on health funding.
senses.exampleCN: 各党在医疗拨款上出现了共同立场。
senses.why: politics uses the word precisely when rivals stop contesting an issue, which is agreement seen as a truce.
senses.whyCN: 政界在对手停止争夺某议题时才用这个词，那是把一致看作停战。

senses.title: A process short of unanimity
senses.titleCN: 不要求全体赞成的一致程序
senses.definition: a decision method in which no one blocks a proposal, though not everyone need approve it
senses.definitionCN: 一种决定方式：无人阻止提议，尽管并非人人都赞成
senses.example: Consensus decision-making does not mean everyone must agree.
senses.exampleCN: 共识决策并不等于人人都必须赞成。
senses.why: groups that cannot afford majority rule redefine consensus as the absence of objection, and the noun follows them.
senses.whyCN: 无法承受多数决的团体，把共识重新定义为「无人反对」，这个名词也跟着这样用。

senses.title: The averaged professional forecast
senses.titleCN: 市场或预测中的平均预期
senses.definition: the central estimate that analysts or forecasters collectively expect
senses.definitionCN: 分析师或预测者集体预期的中心估计
senses.example: The consensus forecast puts growth at two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 市场平均预期把增长定在百分之二。
senses.why: finance takes the many separate views and treats their middle as one voice, which is consensus by aggregation.
senses.whyCN: 金融界把许多分散的看法取其中间，当作一个声音，这是靠汇总得到的共识。

intro.en: Consensus is a Latin noun built on consentire 'to feel together', from com- 'together' and sentire 'to feel'. English borrowed it in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consensus 是一个拉丁名词，出自 consentire「一同感受」，由 com-「共同」与 sentire「感受」构成。英语在十七世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think', and it also gives English sense, sentiment and sentence through related Latin forms.
items.cn: sentire 意为「感觉、知觉、思考」，它还经相关的拉丁形式衍生出英语的 sense、sentiment 与 sentence。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire produced consentire, 'to feel together, to be of one mind, to agree'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire 构成 consentire，意为「一同感受、心意相同、同意」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun consensus named the state of feeling together: agreement, accord, harmony.
items.cn: 第四变格法名词 consensus 命名「一同感受」的状态：一致、和谐、同心。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century, first in learned writing about the body and about philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最初见于关于身体与哲学的学术写作。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries it meant general agreement in any group, and later produced the political phrase consensus politics.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，它指任何群体中的普遍一致，后来又产生「共识政治」这一说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest English example is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the deeper pre-Latin shape of sentire is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对最早的英语书证年代说法不一；sentire 在拉丁语之前的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like consensus but belong to other Latin families; group two holds nouns for collective agreement, each with a different width.
note.cn: 第一组收形似 consensus、却属于别的拉丁词族的词；第二组收表示集体一致的名词，覆盖面各不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin censere 'to assess, estimate', the verb behind censorship and censor: a counting of the population, not a state of agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 censere「评估、估算」，也是 censorship 与 censor 背后的动词：指人口清点，而非意见一致。

entries.definition: Built on the same consentire, but it names permission given by one party rather than agreement across a group.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 consentire，但它指一方给出的许可，而非一群人的普遍一致。

entries.definition: The adjective of this noun: resting on mutual consent, used of contracts, relations and shared reality.
entries.definitionCN: 本名词的形容词：以双方同意为基础，用于合同、关系与共同认定的现实。

entries.definition: A compound naming the work of bringing a group to a shared position before a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词构成的复合词，指在决定之前把一群人带到共同立场的工作。

entries.definition: Complete agreement of all members; consensus can exist without every member approving.
entries.definitionCN: 全体成员完全一致；而 consensus 可以在并非人人赞成时存在。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between parties, often states; it is an instrument, where consensus is a state of mind.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式协定，常指国家间；它是一份文书，而 consensus 是一种心态。

entries.definition: The part of a question on which opponents already agree; it need not cover the whole issue.
entries.definitionCN: 争论各方已经同意的那一部分；它不必覆盖整个议题。

entries.definition: The opinion held by more than half; it is a matter of numbers, whereas consensus is a matter of acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过半数持有的意见；它靠数人头，而 consensus 靠接受程度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire 'feel': to feel together, hence to agree.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire「感受」：一同感受，因而同意。

normal.en: The family runs consensus, consensual, consent, consenting, consensus-building.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 consensus、consensual、consent、consenting、consensus-building。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the scale: broad consensus, scientific consensus, the consensus view.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出规模：广泛共识、科学共识、主流看法。

normal.en: The plural is consensuses, since the Latin fourth-declension ending does not survive in English.
normal.cn: 复数是 consensuses，因为拉丁第四变格法的词尾在英语中没有保留。

normal.en: The near relative census comes from a different verb and means a count, not an agreement.
normal.cn: 形近的 census 出自另一个动词，意为清点，而非一致。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs in which every person finally leans the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，最后每个人都朝同一个方向倾身。

abstract.en: Picture many small streams joining into one wide, slow river.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小溪汇成一条宽而缓的河。

abstract.en: Picture a room going quiet not because anyone was silenced but because no one wished to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子安静下来，不是有人被制止，而是无人再想开口。

examples.en: No consensus emerged, so the chair postponed the vote.
examples.cn: 没有形成共识，于是主席推迟了表决。

examples.en: The consensus among clinicians is to wait another week.
examples.cn: 临床医生之间的共识是再等一周。

examples.en: Consensus in a large group often hides two or three determined minorities.
examples.cn: 大团体里的共识，常常掩盖着两三个坚定的少数派。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ sensus（感觉）」——大家感觉一样 → 共识

root: 拉丁 consensus「一致」出自 consentire「一同感受」= com-（共同）+ sentire（感受）；英语十七世纪借入，最初用于生理与哲学论述。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a room reaching agreement to a market averaging forecasts: the same noun covers a feeling shared by bodies, by committees, by experts and by traders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一间屋子里达成一致，一直到市场把预测取平均：同一个名词涵盖身体、委员会、专家与交易者所共享的那种「同感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people at one table, every hand finally resting on the same sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈人围着一张桌子，最后所有手都落在同一张纸上。

branches.en: THE ROOM: agreement in a group, produced by talk rather than by a count.
branches.cn: 会场：群体中的一致，由谈话而非计数产生。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the prevailing view, and the settled judgement of specialists.
branches.cn: 领域：占上风的看法，以及专家已定下的判断。

branches.en: THE BODY: the oldest loan sense, where organs are said to feel together.
branches.cn: 身体：最早的借入义，器官被说成一同感受。

branches.en: POLITICS: rivals stop contesting, and a process treats silence as consent.
branches.cn: 政治：对手停止争夺，而某种程序把沉默当作同意。

branches.en: THE MARKET: many forecasts averaged into one voice.
branches.cn: 市场：许多预测被平均成一个声音。

intro.en: Consensus is a Latin noun whose prefix and root both survive in English, so the whole word can be read as 'feeling together'.
intro.cn: consensus 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根都留存于英语，因此整词可以读作「一同感受」。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire gives sense, sentiment, consent and consensus, while com- adds the sense of doing something together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 衍生 sense、sentiment、consent 与 consensus，而 com- 增添「共同」之意。

items.example: The prefix makes the feeling shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「感受」成为共享的。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of feeling.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「感受」的意思。

items.example: The verb underlies both consent and consensus.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 consent 与 consensus 的共同底子。

items.example: The committee reached a consensus.
items.exampleCN: 委员会达成了共识。

items.example: The contract is consensual.
items.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同。

items.structure: com- + sentire, as a noun and verb
items.example: She gave her consent in writing.
items.exampleCN: 她以书面形式表示同意。

items.example: The consenting parties signed separately.
items.exampleCN: 表示同意的各方分别签署。

items.example: Consensus-building took most of the week.
items.exampleCN: 凝聚共识占了这一周的大部分时间。

items.example: The word has a narrow sense here.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在这里是窄义。

items.example: Public sentiment turned against the plan.
items.exampleCN: 公众情绪转而反对该方案。

definition_zh: 双方同意的；合意的；（法律）仅以合意成立的
definition_en: resting on the agreement of the people involved, or formed by consent alone without further formality
core_image: 同一张纸的两栏各有一个签名，没有人站在身后催促
scene: 合同末尾的两栏签名都是自愿写下的，桌边没有第三个人。The contract is consensual, so either party may end it by giving notice.
sceneCN: 这里 consensual 指「只凭当事人同意即成立」（第 2 个义项：法律上仅以合意成立的合同）；句意为这是一份合意合同，任何一方通知即可终止。可辨识物件：两栏签名、合同纸、桌边的空椅、钢笔。

senses.title: Resting on mutual agreement
senses.definition: of an arrangement, based on the agreement of everyone involved rather than on force or decree
senses.definitionCN: 指某种安排建立在所有相关方同意之上，而非靠强制或命令
senses.example: The settlement was consensual, not imposed by the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这项和解是双方同意的，并非法院强加。
senses.why: the adjective turns the noun for shared feeling into a property of arrangements: what rests on consent is consensual.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把表示「同感」的名词变成安排的一种性质：建立在同意之上的，就是 consensual。

senses.title: A contract formed by consent alone
senses.titleCN: 仅凭合意即成立的合同
senses.definition: in civil law, of a contract that arises from the parties' agreement without delivery or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在大陆法系中，指无需交付或仪式、仅由当事人合意即成立的合同
senses.example: The contract is consensual, so either party may end it by giving notice.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同，任何一方通知即可终止。
senses.why: law divides contracts by what makes them binding, and consent alone is one of those makers.
senses.whyCN: 法律按「什么使合同有约束力」来分类，而仅有同意就是其中一种来源。

senses.title: Sexual activity with consent
senses.definition: of sexual activity, engaged in with the free agreement of those taking part
senses.definitionCN: 指性行为是在参与者自由同意之下发生的
senses.example: The film portrays a consensual relationship between two adults.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片描绘两个成年人之间自愿的关系。
senses.why: modern law and public speech needed a clear adjective to separate agreement from assault, and this one was chosen.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律与公共讨论需要一个清楚的形容词，把「同意」与「侵犯」分开，选中的就是它。

senses.title: Accepted across a group
senses.definition: of a decision or a norm, accepted by all the parties concerned
senses.definitionCN: 指某项决定或规范被所有相关方接受
senses.example: The change was consensual across all departments.
senses.exampleCN: 这项变动在所有部门都获得了认可。
senses.why: when consent spreads from two people to a whole body, the adjective describes the breadth of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 当同意从两个人扩展到整个机构，这个形容词描述的就是接受的广度。

senses.title: A reality a community shares
senses.definition: in psychology, of what a community treats as real because its members agree on it
senses.definitionCN: 心理学用语：一个群体因其成员一致认可而视为真实的东西
senses.example: Consensual reality is what a community treats as real.
senses.exampleCN: 所谓共同认定的现实，就是一个群体当作真实的东西。
senses.why: psychology asks what makes something real for people, and shared agreement is one of the answers.
senses.whyCN: 心理学追问「对人而言什么算真实」，而共同的同意正是答案之一。

senses.title: A reflex on the other side
senses.titleCN: 医学上对侧的同感反应
senses.definition: in medicine, of a reaction in one part of the body that follows a stimulus applied to the other side
senses.definitionCN: 医学用语：身体一侧受刺激后，另一侧出现的相应反应
senses.example: The pupil shows a consensual reaction to light in the other eye.
senses.exampleCN: 一只眼受光时，另一只眼的瞳孔会出现同感反应。
senses.why: the oldest borrowed sense survives in clinical language, where two sides of the body are said to feel together.
senses.whyCN: 最早的借入义在临床用语中留存：身体两侧被说成「一同感受」。

senses.title: Voluntary rather than forced
senses.definition: of an individual's participation, given freely and without pressure
senses.definitionCN: 指个人的参与出于自由意志，没有受压
senses.example: Participation in the survey was consensual and anonymous.
senses.exampleCN: 参与这项调查是自愿且匿名的。
senses.why: the focus shifts from the arrangement to the person: nothing was taken from anyone without a yes.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从「安排」移到「人」：没有在缺少一个「愿意」的情况下从任何人那里拿走什么。

senses.title: Settled by convention, not by proof
senses.titleCN: 靠约定而非靠论证确定
senses.definition: of a definition or a standard, fixed by shared usage rather than by authority or demonstration
senses.definitionCN: 指定义或标准由共同用法确定，而非由权威或证明确定
senses.example: The boundary of the term is consensual among practitioners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个术语的边界在从业者之间是约定俗成的。
senses.why: some questions cannot be proved, only agreed, and the adjective marks that kind of settlement.
senses.whyCN: 有些问题无法证明，只能约定，这个形容词标记的正是这类了结方式。

intro.en: Consensual is built on the Latin noun consensus 'agreement' plus the adjective ending -al, which continues Latin -alis. Its root is sentire 'to feel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consensual 由拉丁名词 consensus「一致」加形容词词尾 -al 构成，后者延续拉丁 -alis。其词根是 sentire「感受」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think'; it is the root behind sense, sentiment, consent and consensus.
items.cn: sentire 意为「感觉、知觉、思考」，是 sense、sentiment、consent 与 consensus 共同的词根。

items.en: The noun consensus, from consentire 'to feel together', named agreement or accord as a state.
items.cn: 名词 consensus 出自 consentire「一同感受」，命名作为状态的「一致」或「同心」。

items.en: The ending -alis formed adjectives of relation, as in naturalis and legalis; English keeps it as -al.
items.cn: 词尾 -alis 构成表示关系的形容词，如 naturalis 与 legalis；英语以 -al 保留它。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the eighteenth century, first in legal and philosophical writing about agreements and shared perception.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪出现于英语，最初见于论述协议与共同感知的法律、哲学文字。

items.en: Psychologists extended it to shared reality, physicians kept it for sympathetic reflexes, and modern law applied it to sexual consent.
items.cn: 心理学家把它扩展到共同认定的现实，医生把它保留给同感反射，现代法律则把它用于性方面的同意。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and formation): dictionaries date the first English use differently, and it is unsettled whether the word was coined in English or already existed in medieval Latin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与构词地）：各家词典对最早的英语用例说法不一，也无法确定这个词是在英语中造出，还是中古拉丁语里已有。

note.en: Group one holds words close in shape, one of which shares the root but not the meaning; group two holds adjectives for what people freely accept.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的词，其中一个与本词同根而不同义；第二组收表示「人们自愿接受」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective comes from: general agreement in a group.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词所出的名词：群体中的普遍一致。

entries.definition: Also from consentire, but it names permission itself, and it is a noun and a verb, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 consentire，但它命名许可本身，且是名词与动词，不是形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin sensualis, built on sensus 'sense, feeling': it means devoted to bodily pleasure, not based on agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sensualis，由 sensus「感觉」构成；意为沉于肉体享乐，与「同意」无关。

entries.definition: From censere 'to assess': a population count; it looks close but belongs to another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 censere「评估」：人口清点；形近，却属于另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Done by one's own choice; it stresses the absence of compulsion rather than the presence of two agreeing parties.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自己选择而做；侧重「无强制」，而非「两方相合」。

entries.definition: Held or done by each toward the other; a mutual feeling need not be formally agreed.
entries.definitionCN: 双方各自对对方持有或做出的；相互的情感不必经过正式同意。

entries.definition: Created by or arising from a contract; it needs a document, where consensual needs only assent.
entries.definitionCN: 由合同产生或与合同有关；它需要一份文书，而 consensual 只需要同意。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule or an authority; permissible is about permission from above, consensual about agreement between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 为规则或权威所允许；permissible 关乎自上而下的许可，consensual 关乎平辈之间的同意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Consensus plus -al: the adjective of the shared feeling.
normal.cn: consensus 加 -al：把「共同感受」变成形容词。

normal.en: The family runs consensus, consensual, consensually, consent, consenting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 consensus、consensual、consensually、consent、consenting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its fields: a consensual contract, a consensual relationship, consensual reality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的领域：合意合同、双方自愿的关系、共同认定的现实。

normal.en: The medical phrase consensual reflex survives from the oldest sense of the root.
normal.cn: 医学上的「同感反射」一语，源自这个词根最古老的一义。

normal.en: The opposite is non-consensual, common in law and in policy.
normal.cn: 相反的说法是 non-consensual，在法律与政策文本中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture two signatures on one sheet with nobody standing behind the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸上有两个签名，笔后没有站着任何人。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when both handles are turned.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有两个把手同时转动才开的门。

abstract.en: Picture two people letting go of a rope at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同时松开同一条绳。

examples.en: A consensual separation avoids the cost and bitterness of a trial.
examples.cn: 合意分居省去了诉讼的花费与怨气。

examples.en: The guild's standards are consensual rather than legally enforced.
examples.cn: 行会的标准靠约定，而非靠法律强制。

examples.en: Consensual decision-making can stall when one member refuses to move.
examples.cn: 只要有一名成员不肯动，共识决策就可能卡住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ sens（感觉）+ ual」——大家感觉一样、都点头 → 合意的

root: 拉丁 consensus「一致」+ -alis（关系形容词词尾）→ 英语 consensual；词根 sentire「感受」，com- 表「共同」，故本义为「一同感受而同意」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on a yes that was freely given: to a contract, to a relationship, to a group norm, to a shared reality, to a clinical reaction, to participation, or to a definition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个自由给出的「愿意」上：对合同、对关系、对群体规范、对共同认定的现实、对临床反应、对参与，或对一个定义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on one sheet, with no third person standing behind the pen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸上有两个签名，笔后没有第三人站着。

branches.en: THE FREELY GIVEN YES: what rests on agreement, and the person who was not pressed.
branches.cn: 自由的愿意：建立在同意之上的安排，以及没有被压的人。

branches.en: LAW WITHOUT FORM: consent alone makes the contract binding.
branches.cn: 无需形式的法律：仅有同意就使合同生效。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES DRAWN BY AGREEMENT: sexual consent, and a term fixed by usage rather than proof.
branches.cn: 靠同意划出的边界：性方面的同意，以及靠用法而非证明定下的术语。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BODY: consent spreads from two parties to every department.
branches.cn: 整个机构：同意从两方扩展到每个部门。

branches.en: SHARED INNER AND OUTER LIFE: a community's reality, and one side of a body answering the other.
branches.cn: 内与外的共享：群体的现实，以及身体一侧回应另一侧。

intro.en: Consensual is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective ending; both parts recur throughout English academic vocabulary.
intro.cn: consensual 是一个拉丁名词加一个拉丁形容词词尾，两部分在英语学术词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire supplies the root, consensus supplies the noun, and -alis supplies the relational adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 提供词根，consensus 提供名词，-alis 提供关系形容词词尾。
