items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使感受成为共享的。

items.example: The root carries the idea of feeling.
items.exampleCN: 词根带着「感受」的意思。

items.example: The word arrived from Latin whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词整体来自拉丁语。

items.example: The ending turns a noun into a relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成关系形容词。

items.example: The contract is consensual.
items.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同。

items.example: The terms were consensually adopted.
items.exampleCN: 条款经双方同意获得通过。

items.example: She gave consent in writing.
items.exampleCN: 她书面表示同意。

items.example: The law targets non-consensual sharing of images.
items.exampleCN: 该法律针对未经同意传播影像的行为。

items.example: The phrase has a technical sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语有技术上的含义。

definition_zh: 妥协；折中；折中方案；危及；使受损
definition_en: a settlement in which each side gives up something, or to settle in that way, or to expose something to risk
core_image: 两个人各交出半张地图，拼成一幅不完整却够用的图
scene: 会议室里，双方各自划掉自己最想要的那一条，留下的版本谁都不完全满意。After a long night, the two delegations reached a compromise on the disputed border.
sceneCN: 这里 compromise 指「各方各让一步而达成的安排」（第 1 个义项：折中式的和解）；句意为熬过漫长的一夜，两国代表团就有争议的边界达成了折中方案。可辨识物件：被划掉的条款、两份地图、冷掉的咖啡、签字笔。

pos.zh: （债务）折偿安排；（旧）提交仲裁的合意
以让步解决；危及；使受损

derivatives.zh: 有损声誉的；危及安全的

senses.title: A settlement by mutual concession
senses.definition: an agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wanted
senses.definitionCN: 各方都放弃一部分所求而达成的协议
senses.example: After a long night, the two delegations reached a compromise on the disputed border.
senses.exampleCN: 熬过漫长的一夜，两国代表团就有争议的边界达成了折中方案。
senses.why: the Latin source named a mutual promise, and the modern sense keeps the mutuality while changing the object from promise to concession.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源指的是「相互许诺」，现代义保留了「相互」，只是对象从「许诺」换成了「让步」。

senses.title: The middle course itself
senses.titleCN: 折中出来的那个中间版本
senses.definition: the resulting arrangement, which satisfies neither side completely
senses.definitionCN: 由此得到的安排，双方都不完全满意
senses.example: The new timetable is a compromise between speed and cost.
senses.exampleCN: 新的时间表是速度与成本之间的折中。
senses.why: English often names the product by the act that made it, so the settlement and its terms share one word.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用「造出它的动作」来命名产物，因此和解与其条款共用同一个词。

senses.title: Exposure to danger or discredit
senses.titleCN: 使安全或名誉受到暴露
senses.definition: the state of being put at risk, as of security, a case or a reputation
senses.definitionCN: 被置于风险之中的状态，如安全、案件或名誉
senses.example: The leak was a serious compromise of national security.
senses.exampleCN: 这次泄露严重危及国家安全。
senses.why: a compromise lets something be weakened in exchange for something else, and the noun extended from deals to damage.
senses.whyCN: 折中意味着以某物的削弱换取另一物，这个名词便从「交易」扩展到「损害」。

senses.title: A debt settled for less
senses.definition: in insolvency, an arrangement by which creditors accept less than they are owed
senses.definitionCN: 在破产事务中，债权人接受少于债权的清偿安排
senses.example: The creditors accepted a compromise of fifty pence in the pound.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人接受了每镑偿付五十便士的折偿方案。
senses.why: a composition with creditors is literally a bargain over a debt, which is why the older commercial word fits.
senses.whyCN: 与债权人的债务折偿，字面上就是围绕一笔债的讨价还价，因此这个较早的商业词正合用。

senses.title: Submission of a case to an arbiter
senses.definition: the older legal sense of binding oneself to accept an arbitrator's decision
senses.definitionCN: 较老的法律义：约束自己接受仲裁人的裁断
senses.example: The parties entered a compromise of their case before the bishop.
senses.exampleCN: 双方把争议提交主教仲裁。
senses.why: this is the original sense of the Latin word: a mutual promise to abide by a third party's ruling.
senses.whyCN: 这正是这个拉丁词的原始义：相互许诺服从第三方的裁断。

senses.title: To settle by concession
senses.definition: of the verb, to end a dispute by each side giving ground
senses.definitionCN: 指动词义：各方各自退让，把争执了结
senses.example: The two sides compromised on the number of inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在检查员人数上各让一步。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into action, and it can be used of one party yielding as well.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把名词化为动作，也可以只指一方让步。

senses.title: To put something at risk
senses.definition: of the verb, to weaken or endanger something by an unwise act
senses.definitionCN: 指动词义：因不当之举削弱或危及某物
senses.example: One careless email compromised the whole investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 一封不慎的邮件危及了整个调查。
senses.why: what has been bargained away can also be a safeguard, so the verb came to mean exposing a protection.
senses.whyCN: 被「换掉」的东西也可能是保护措施，于是这个动词也指「使防护暴露」。

senses.title: To damage one's standing
senses.titleCN: 损害自己的立场或名誉
senses.definition: of the verb, to bring a person or an institution into discredit
senses.definitionCN: 指动词义：使某人或某机构陷入名誉受损的境地
senses.example: He compromised himself by accepting the gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他收下那份礼物，使自己陷入了不名誉的境地。
senses.why: reputation behaves like security: once weakened, it can be exploited by others.
senses.whyCN: 名誉像安全一样：一旦被削弱，就可能被别人利用。

senses.title: To dilute a design or a standard
senses.titleCN: 削弱设计或标准的品质
senses.definition: of the verb, to lower the quality of something by accepting a weaker version
senses.definitionCN: 指动词义：接受了较弱的版本，因而降低某物的品质
senses.example: The revised engine was compromised by too little testing.
senses.exampleCN: 改款的发动机因测试不足而打了折扣。
senses.why: an engineering compromise is a concession made inside the object rather than between people.
senses.whyCN: 工程上的「折中」，是在物件内部而不是在人与人之间作出的让步。

intro.en: Compromise came from Old French compromis, from Latin compromissum, a mutual promise, built on com- 'together' and promittere 'to promise'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: compromise 来自古法语 compromis，出自拉丁 compromissum「相互的许诺」，由 com-「共同」与 promittere「许诺」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, to let go'. Its compounds carry the idea of sending something forward or out.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」。它的复合词都带有「把某物送向前或送出去」的意思。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus mittere produced promittere, 'to promise', literally to send one's word forward.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 mittere 构成 promittere「许诺」，字面是「把自己的话送出去」。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus promittere gave compromittere, 'to promise mutually', especially to bind oneself to accept an arbiter's award.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 promittere 得出 compromittere「相互许诺」，尤指约束自己接受仲裁人的裁断。

items.en: Old French compromis named the mutual engagement itself, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century with that legal sense.
items.cn: 古法语 compromis 命名这种相互约束本身，英语在十四世纪借入时正是这个法律义。

items.en: By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the word had shifted from submitting to an arbiter to settling by each side giving ground.
items.cn: 到十七、十八世纪，这个词从「服从仲裁」转为「各方让步而了结」。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact decade in which the concession sense displaced the arbitration sense is not fixed, and the further history of mittere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：「让步」义取代「仲裁」义的确切年代并无定论；mittere 更早的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same promise root or resembling it on the page; group two holds nouns and verbs for settling or for damaging.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「许诺」词根、或纸面上形近的词；第二组收表示「了结」与「损害」的名词与动词。

entries.definition: From promittere without the prefix: a pledge given by one party, with no mutual concession implied.
entries.definitionCN: 出自不带前缀的 promittere：一方给出的承诺，不含相互让步。

entries.definition: From comprehendere 'to grasp together', built on prehendere 'to seize': to consist of, not to settle by concession.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 comprehendere「一并抓住」，由 prehendere「抓取」构成：意为包含，而非以让步了结。

entries.definition: The present participle used as an adjective: damaging to reputation or safety rather than willing to concede.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词转作形容词：指有损名誉或安全，而不是愿意让步。

entries.definition: With un-: refusing to concede anything, often used of firm stands and stern weather.
entries.definitionCN: 加 un-：拒绝任何让步，常用于坚定的立场与严酷的天气。

entries.definition: Something yielded by one party; a compromise is the whole settlement built from such yields.
entries.definitionCN: 一方让出的东西；而 compromise 是由这些让出拼成的整个安排。

entries.definition: The formal end of a dispute; it names the close, not the mutual giving that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 争端的正式结束；它命名的是收尾，而非促成收尾的相互让步。

entries.definition: A balance in which gaining one thing costs another; it is a calculation, where compromise is a negotiation.
entries.definitionCN: 得到一样就要失去另一样的权衡；它是计算，而 compromise 是谈判。

entries.definition: To put at risk; it matches only the damaging branch of compromise, with no bargaining in it.
entries.definitionCN: 使陷入危险；只对应 compromise 的损害那一支，不含谈判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus promittere 'promise': a promise made by both sides.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 promittere「许诺」：双方一起作出的许诺。

normal.en: The family runs compromise, compromising, compromised, uncompromising, compromiser.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compromise、compromising、compromised、uncompromising、compromiser。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both branches: reach a compromise, compromise safety.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两支：达成折中、危及安全。

normal.en: The adjective uncompromising means the opposite of willing to concede.
normal.cn: 形容词 uncompromising 意为「不肯让步」，正好相反。

normal.en: The related verb promise keeps the root without the prefix of togetherness.
normal.cn: 同根的动词 promise 保留词根，却没有「共同」这一前缀。

abstract.en: Picture two half maps laid edge to edge, neither one complete.
abstract.cn: 想象两张半幅地图边对边拼起，没有一张是完整的。

abstract.en: Picture a scale in which both pans are lowered at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两个秤盘同时下沉。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with one brick removed so that a door can be cut.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上抽掉一块砖，好开出一扇门。

examples.en: They compromised on the price rather than lose the order.
examples.cn: 他们在价格上让了一步，以免丢掉订单。

examples.en: A single weak password can compromise an entire network.
examples.cn: 一个弱口令就足以危及整个网络。

examples.en: The plan was a compromise between the engineers and the accountants.
examples.cn: 这个方案是工程师与会计两方折中的产物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（共同）+ promise（许诺）」——双方共同许下各让一步的诺 → 妥协

root: 拉丁 compromittere「相互许诺」= com-（共同）+ promittere（许诺，pro- 向前 + mittere 送出）；原义为提交仲裁的约定，十七八世纪转为「各让一步」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start from a mutual promise and split two ways: toward settlement by concession, and toward exposure to risk, since what is bargained away can also be a safeguard.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「相互许诺」出发，分成两条路：一条走向「各让一步」，一条走向「暴露于风险」，因为被让出去的东西也可能是保护措施。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people each handing over half a map to make one usable, incomplete map.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人各交出半幅地图，拼成一幅够用却不完整的地图。

branches.en: THE DEAL AND ITS SHAPE: the settlement, and the middle version it produces.
branches.cn: 交易与其形状：和解本身，以及它造出的中间版本。

branches.en: REPUTATION AT STAKE: security and personal standing can both be weakened.
branches.cn: 名誉涉险：安全与个人立场都可能被削弱。

branches.en: DEBT BARGAINED DOWN: creditors accept less, which is a compromise in the oldest commercial sense.
branches.cn: 债务被压低：债权人少收，这是最老商业意义上的折中。

branches.en: THE ARBITER'S AWARD: the original sense, kept in older legal writing.
branches.cn: 仲裁人的裁断：原始义，保存在较早的法律文字中。

branches.en: THE VERB'S RANGE: people settle, things get put at risk, and engineers settle inside the object.
branches.cn: 动词的范围：人与人相互了结，也可能把某物置于风险，工程师则在物件内部作取舍。

intro.en: Compromise is a Latin compound of a prefix of togetherness and a verb of sending, so its parts read as 'send a promise together'.
intro.cn: compromise 是一个拉丁复合词，由「共同」前缀与「送出」动词构成，两部分连起来可读作「一起送出许诺」。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere yields promise, compromise, permit and transmit, while com- adds the sense of doing something jointly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 promise、compromise、permit 与 transmit，而 com- 增添「共同」之意。

items.example: The prefix makes the promise mutual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使许诺成为相互的。

items.example: The root carries the idea of sending forth.
items.exampleCN: 词根带着「送出去」的意思。

items.example: The verb sends one's word forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把话送向前方。

items.example: The compound began in arbitration.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词起于仲裁场合。

items.example: They reached a compromise.
items.exampleCN: 他们达成了折中方案。

items.example: The photographs were compromising.
items.exampleCN: 那些照片很能坏人事。

items.example: The system was compromised.
items.exampleCN: 系统已被攻破。

items.example: He was called a compromiser.
items.exampleCN: 他被人称作凡事好商量的人。

items.example: Her uncompromising tone ended the talks.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不让步的语气终止了会谈。

items.example: He kept his promise.
items.exampleCN: 他守住了承诺。

latinEntries.meaning: a mutual promise, a arbitration agreement

definition_zh: 有损声誉的；令人难堪的；危及安全的；（罕）愿意让步的
definition_en: revealing something damaging or exposing someone to risk, and rarely, willing to settle by concession
core_image: 一张被拍到的照片，桌上摊着本不该出现的文件
scene: 记者的相机里有一段录像，画面中的人正把一份本不该带出的文件放回包里。The newspaper refused to publish the compromising photographs until the case was closed.
sceneCN: 这里 compromising 指「一旦公开就会损害当事人声誉」（第 1 个义项：有损名誉的）；句意为报社拒绝在案件了结之前发表那些令人难堪的照片。可辨识物件：相机、录像画面、文件、公文包。

pos.zh: 有损声誉的；令人难堪的
危及安全的；削弱主张的

collocations.zh: 一旦曝光就难堪的处境
在政治上会带来麻烦的

derivatives.zh: 以损害声誉的方式（罕用）

senses.title: Damaging to a reputation
senses.titleCN: 有损名誉、一旦公开就难堪
senses.definition: of a photograph, letter or fact, likely to bring a person into discredit if known
senses.definitionCN: 指照片、信件或事实一旦被人知道，就可能使某人名誉受损
senses.example: The newspaper refused to publish the compromising photographs until the case was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 报社拒绝在案件了结之前发表那些令人难堪的照片。
senses.why: the participle inherits the verb's risk sense: what compromises a person is compromising.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词继承了动词的「风险」义：会危及某人的东西，就是 compromising。

senses.title: Incriminating in substance
senses.titleCN: 内容本身构成不利证据
senses.definition: of a document or a recording, containing material that suggests wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 指文件或录音中含有暗示不当行为的材料
senses.example: The auditors found compromising entries in the ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员在账簿里发现了不利的条目。
senses.why: reputation damage and legal exposure overlap: the same paper can end a career and start a case.
senses.whyCN: 名誉受损与法律风险彼此重叠：同一张纸可以毁掉前程，也可以开出一桩案子。

senses.title: Risky for security
senses.definition: of a practice or a fault, likely to weaken a system's protection
senses.definitionCN: 指某种做法或缺陷可能削弱系统的防护
senses.example: A compromising default setting left the server open.
senses.exampleCN: 一个危及安全的默认设置让服务器敞开了。
senses.why: the engineering branch of compromise produces an adjective for whatever introduces the weakness.
senses.whyCN: compromise 在工程上的那一支，造出一个形容词，用来指任何引入弱点的东西。

senses.title: Weakening a case in argument
senses.definition: of a fact or an admission, tending to make a claim less credible
senses.definitionCN: 指某事实或某项承认，会使某个主张的可信度下降
senses.example: The delay was compromising for the whole theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这段延迟对整个理论都构成削弱。
senses.why: a case is like a structure: it can be undermined by one weak point, and the adjective marks that point.
senses.whyCN: 一个论点就像一座结构：一个薄弱点就能把它掏空，这个形容词标记的正是那个点。

senses.title: Awkward if seen
senses.titleCN: 被人看见就会解释不清的处境
senses.definition: of a position or a meeting, hard to explain and therefore embarrassing
senses.definitionCN: 指某种处境或会面难以解释，因而令人尴尬
senses.example: They were found in a compromising position in the archive room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人发现他们在档案室里，情形很难解释清楚。
senses.why: this is the reputation sense narrowed to a scene rather than a document.
senses.whyCN: 这是名誉义收窄到「一个场面」，而非一份文件。

senses.title: Willing to give ground
senses.definition: of a person or a mood, ready to settle by concession rather than insist
senses.definitionCN: 指人或情绪愿意以让步了结，而不坚持到底
senses.example: A compromising tone in the letter suggested room to negotiate.
senses.exampleCN: 信里那种肯商量的语气，暗示还有谈的余地。
senses.why: the rare adjective reading is the plain one: showing a disposition to compromise.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕见的形容词义其实最直白：显示出愿意妥协的倾向。

senses.title: Harmful to trust
senses.definition: of a disclosure or a rumour, likely to damage a relationship between people or bodies
senses.definitionCN: 指某项披露或传言可能损害个人或机构之间的信任关系
senses.example: The rumour was compromising for both governments.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言对两国政府都有损害。
senses.why: trust is a shared asset, so anything that weakens it is compromising to both holders.
senses.whyCN: 信任是双方共有的资产，削弱它的东西，对两边都构成损害。

senses.title: Lowering a standard
senses.definition: of a shortcut or a revision, reducing the quality that a thing was meant to have
senses.definitionCN: 指某种捷径或修改，降低了事物本应具备的品质
senses.example: The cheaper alloy was compromising for the whole design.
senses.exampleCN: 那种更便宜的合金拖累了整个设计。
senses.why: the engineering sense of a diluted standard, dressed as an adjective for the cause.
senses.whyCN: 这是「标准被稀释」的工程义，以形容词形式指向那个原因。

intro.en: Compromising is the present participle of compromise, whose Latin source compromittere meant to promise mutually; the damaging sense grew in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: compromising 是 compromise 的现在分词，后者的拉丁源头 compromittere 意为「相互许诺」；指「损害」的义项在十七世纪发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, to let go', and it supplies the second half of the compound.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，是这个复合词的后一半。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus promittere 'to promise' produced the verb for binding oneself mutually, first in arbitration.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 promittere「许诺」构成这个动词，表示相互约束，最初用于仲裁。

items.en: English developed the sense 'to expose to risk or discredit', and the participle followed, describing whatever causes that exposure.
items.cn: 英语发展出「使陷入风险或名誉受损」义，分词随后跟进，用来描述造成这种暴露的东西。

items.en: The adjective settled into phrases about papers, positions and letters, the ordinary stock of scandal and litigation.
items.cn: 这个形容词固定出现在关于文件、处境与信件的说法里，那正是丑闻与诉讼的日常材料。

items.en: Photography and then computing widened its range: a compromising picture, a compromising configuration.
items.cn: 摄影、以及后来的计算机，拓宽了它的范围：会坏事的照片、会出事的配置。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact decade when the adjective began to mean damaging is unsettled, and the further history of the sending root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个形容词开始表示「有损」的确切年代没有定论；「送出」词根更早的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb or of confusing near-forms; group two holds adjectives that also describe what harms a person or a case.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个动词的各种形式、以及容易混淆的近形词；第二组收同样描述「损害某人或某事」的形容词。

entries.definition: The past participle: already weakened or breached, describing the victim rather than the thing that did the damage.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词：已经被削弱或攻破，描述受害者，而不是造成损害的东西。

entries.definition: Built on promittere like compromise, but without com-: it means giving grounds for hope, not grounds for scandal.
entries.definitionCN: 与 compromise 同出 promittere，但没有 com-：意为「有前途」，而非「会出事」。

entries.definition: From comprehendere 'to grasp together': consisting of, a completely different verb behind a similar shape.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 comprehendere「一并抓住」：意为「包含」，相似外形背后是完全不同的动词。

entries.definition: With un-: refusing to concede, which is almost the opposite of the rare willing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 加 un-：拒绝让步，几乎与那个罕见的「愿意让步」义相反。

entries.definition: Showing that someone is guilty of a crime; it covers only the evidence branch of compromising.
entries.definitionCN: 显示某人有罪；只覆盖 compromising 的证据那一支。

entries.definition: Causing awkwardness; it names the feeling, while compromising names the damage that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 造成尴尬；它命名的是感受，而 compromising 命名的是随之而来的损害。

entries.definition: Causing harm of any kind; the widest of the group, with no hint of scandal or security.
entries.definitionCN: 造成任何种类的伤害；本组中范围最广，不带丑闻或安全的暗示。

entries.definition: Bringing shame on a person; it judges conduct, whereas compromising judges the exposure of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人蒙羞；它评判行为，而 compromising 评判证据被暴露的风险。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the verb's present participle, so it names the thing that does the compromising.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是动词的现在分词，因此它命名的是「造成损害的那一方」。

normal.en: The family runs compromise, compromising, compromised, uncompromising, compromiser.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compromise、compromising、compromised、uncompromising、compromiser。

normal.en: Fixed phrases are mostly about paper and scenes: compromising letters, a compromising position.
normal.cn: 固定搭配多与纸面与场面有关：会坏事的信件、难以解释的处境。

normal.en: The negative uncompromising means the opposite: refusing to yield.
normal.cn: 否定的 uncompromising 意为相反：拒绝让步。

normal.en: The related promising shares the promise root but means hopeful, not damaging.
normal.cn: 近形的 promising 同出「许诺」词根，却意为「有前途」，而非「有损」。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph taken at the worst possible moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在最不该按下快门时拍下的照片。

abstract.en: Picture a single loose thread that unravels a whole sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象一根松线把整只袖子拆开。

abstract.en: Picture a key left in a lock overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙整夜留在锁孔里。

examples.en: The minister resigned after compromising letters reached the press.
examples.cn: 那些不利的信件落到媒体手里之后，部长辞职了。

examples.en: No compromising detail was left in the shared folder.
examples.cn: 共享文件夹里没有留下任何会坏事的细节。

examples.en: The report called the loophole compromising for the whole safety system.
examples.cn: 报告称这个漏洞危及整个安全体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「compromise（危及）+ ing」——正在危及名声的那种 → 有损声誉的

root: compromise 的现在分词；compromise 出自拉丁 compromittere「相互许诺」= com-（共同）+ promittere（许诺）；十七世纪发展出「使陷入风险、使名誉受损」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a thing that does damage on exposure: to a name, a case, a system, an argument, a scene, a trust, a standard, or, in the rare reading, a willingness to yield.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「一旦暴露就造成损害」的东西：对名声、案件、系统、论点、场面、信任、标准，或在罕见的读法里，对「愿意让步」的性格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a photograph taken at the worst possible moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：在最不该按下快门的那一刻拍下的一张照片。

branches.en: WHAT THE PAPER DOES: a photograph shames, and a ledger entry incriminates.
branches.cn: 纸面所做的事：照片使人难堪，账簿条目成为罪证。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND STANDARDS: a default setting opens a server, a cheap alloy drags the design down.
branches.cn: 系统与标准：一个默认设置敞开服务器，一种廉价合金拖累设计。

branches.en: ARGUMENTS AND TRUST: a delay weakens a theory, a rumour weakens a relationship.
branches.cn: 论点与信任：一段延迟削弱理论，一则传言削弱关系。

branches.en: THE SCENE: reputation damage narrowed to a moment someone walked in on.
branches.cn: 场面：名誉受损收窄到「有人正好撞见」的一刻。

branches.en: THE RARE READING: the same form can still mean simply ready to concede.
branches.cn: 罕见的读法：同一形式仍可只表示「愿意让步」。

intro.en: Compromising is a participle built on a Latin compound verb, so its prefix, root and ending all carry readable meaning.
intro.cn: compromising 是一个建立在拉丁复合动词上的分词，前缀、词根与词尾都带着可读的意义。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere gives promise, compromise, permit and transmit; com- adds togetherness and -ing adds the ongoing or causative reading.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 promise、compromise、permit 与 transmit；com- 增添「共同」，-ing 增添「正在进行或致成」的读法。

items.example: The prefix makes the promise mutual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使许诺成为相互的。

items.example: The root supplies the sending image.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「送出」的意象。

items.example: The word sends a pledge forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把承诺送向前方。

items.meaning: to settle, to expose to risk
items.example: One email compromised the files.
items.exampleCN: 一封邮件危及了那些文件。

items.example: The ending makes the verb describe a cause.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使动词转而描述一个成因。

items.example: The letters were compromising.
items.exampleCN: 那些信件很能坏人事。

items.example: The account was compromised.
items.exampleCN: 这个账户已被攻破。

items.example: His uncompromising reply ended the exchange.
items.exampleCN: 他毫不让步的答复终止了往来。

items.example: The first results were promising.
items.exampleCN: 最初的结果很有希望。

definition_zh: 合作；协作；（与占领者）通敌；协助
definition_en: to work together with others on a task, or, in a hostile sense, to help an enemy or an occupier
core_image: 两双手在同一架织机上同时操作，各自负责一半
scene: 实验室里，两组人把各自测到的数据摊在同一张大桌上对照。The two universities agreed to collaborate on a study of coastal erosion.
sceneCN: 这里 collaborate 指「两个团队共同完成一项工作」（第 1 个义项：合作共事）；句意为两所大学同意就海岸侵蚀问题合作开展研究。可辨识物件：大桌、两摞数据表、坐标纸、显微镜。

senses.title: Work jointly on a task
senses.definition: to work with one or more others toward a shared result
senses.definitionCN: 与一个或几个人一起朝共同的结果努力
senses.example: The two universities agreed to collaborate on a study of coastal erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学同意就海岸侵蚀问题合作开展研究。
senses.why: the Latin verb joins com- 'together' to laborare 'to work', so the core reading is simply working together.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词把 com-「共同」与 laborare「劳动」接在一起，核心意思就是「一起干活」。

senses.title: Create a work together
senses.definition: of writers, artists or musicians, to produce a work jointly
senses.definitionCN: 指作家、艺术家或音乐家共同产生一件作品
senses.example: The novelist collaborated with a photographer on the book.
senses.exampleCN: 小说家与一位摄影师合作完成了这本书。
senses.why: joint work in the arts is the same act as joint work in a lab, only the product is a work rather than a result.
senses.whyCN: 艺术上的共同劳作与实验室里的共同劳作是同一个动作，只是产物是作品而非结果。

senses.title: Institutions pooling resources
senses.definition: of organizations, to run a programme or a study together
senses.definitionCN: 指机构共同运行一个项目或一项研究
senses.example: Three hospitals collaborated on the vaccine trial.
senses.exampleCN: 三家医院合作开展了疫苗试验。
senses.why: large bodies cannot work side by side, so the verb comes to mean pooling staff, data and money.
senses.whyCN: 大型机构无法并肩干活，于是这个动词转为「共享人力、数据与经费」。

senses.title: Help an occupying enemy
senses.definition: to cooperate with an enemy that has taken control of one's country
senses.definitionCN: 与已经控制本国的敌人合作
senses.example: Those who collaborated with the occupiers faced trial after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 那些与占领者合作的人在战后受到审判。
senses.why: the word for working together darkened in wartime, because working with an occupier is a kind of cooperation too.
senses.whyCN: 「一起干活」这个词在战时变了颜色，因为与占领者一起干活，也是一种合作。

senses.title: Knowingly assist wrongdoing
senses.definition: to give help to a person or a scheme one knows to be harmful
senses.definitionCN: 对明知有害的人或计划提供帮助
senses.example: The clerk was accused of collaborating in the fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员被指控在诈骗中予以协助。
senses.why: help is help whatever the cause, so the negative sense spreads from politics to crime and misconduct.
senses.whyCN: 帮助就是帮助，不论缘由，于是这个负面义从政治扩散到犯罪与不当行为。

senses.title: Cooperate with a request
senses.definition: to go along with someone's plan or request in an ordinary, neutral way
senses.definitionCN: 以平常、中性的方式配合某人的计划或请求
senses.example: The witnesses collaborated fully with the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 证人们全力配合了调查。
senses.why: this is the neutral middle of the word: not a shared project, but not betrayal either.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的中性地带：既不是共同项目，也不是背叛。

senses.title: Work with a rival
senses.definition: to work alongside a competitor on a matter of common interest
senses.definitionCN: 在与竞争对手有共同利益的事项上一起工作
senses.example: Rival airlines collaborated on the safety guidelines.
senses.exampleCN: 相互竞争的航空公司合作制定了安全准则。
senses.why: the word can hold opposites at once: parties stay rivals and still share the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以同时容纳相反的两面：各方仍是竞争对手，却仍分担同一份工作。

senses.title: Systems working in tandem
senses.definition: of software, equipment or teams, to operate together smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 指软件、设备或团队顺畅地一起运作
senses.example: The two programs collaborate through a shared protocol.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个程序通过一套共享协议协同工作。
senses.why: machines are given the human verb when their parts must act as one, the newest branch of the word.
senses.whyCN: 当机器的各部分必须像一体那样行动，就给它用了这个属人的动词，这是最新的一支。

intro.en: Collaborate comes from Latin collaborare, com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work'. English borrowed it in the nineteenth century; the traitorous sense arrived in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaborate 来自拉丁 collaborare，由 com-「共同」与 laborare「劳动」构成。英语在十九世纪借入；「通敌」义在二十世纪四十年代出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'toil, effort, hardship'. Its deeper origin is not established, and forms proposed for it before Latin exist only as reconstructions.
items.cn: labor 意为「辛劳、费力、艰苦」。其更深来源没有定论，为它在拉丁语之前提出的形式只以重构形式存在。

items.en: The verb laborare meant 'to work, toil, suffer hardship', and it also underlies English elaborate and laboratory through related forms.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为「劳作、辛苦、受苦」，它还经相关形式构成英语的 elaborate 与 laboratory。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare produced collaborare, 'to work together', a plain compound with no special legal or political colour.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 laborare 得出 collaborare「一起劳作」，是一个平实的复合词，不带法律或政治色彩。

items.en: English took the verb in the nineteenth century, first in writing about science, literature and public works.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，最初见于关于科学、文学与公共工程的写作。

items.en: In the 1940s the noun was applied to those who cooperated with an occupying power, and the verb took on that stigma.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代，这个名词被用于指与占领当局合作的人，动词也随之带上这层污名。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest English use is dated differently across dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of labor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对最早的英语用例说法不一；labor 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same working root or on similar shapes; group two holds verbs of joint action, from neutral to suspicious.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「劳作」词根或形近的词；第二组收表示共同行动的动词，从中性到可疑。

entries.definition: From e- 'out' plus laborare: to work something out in detail, so it shares the working root but not the togetherness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 e-「向外」加 laborare 构成：把某事做细做透，与「劳作」同根，却没有「共同」之意。

entries.definition: From Latin laborare through a place noun: a room for work, not a act of working with others.
entries.definitionCN: 经一个地点名词出自拉丁 laborare：干活的房间，而不是与他人共同劳作的行为。

entries.definition: From Latin roborare 'to strengthen', built on robur 'oak, strength': to confirm, with no link to working.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 roborare「使强固」，由 robur「橡木、力量」构成：意为证实，与「劳作」无关。

entries.definition: The noun of this verb: joint work, or, in the wartime sense, cooperation with an enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 本动词的名词：共同的工作，或战时意义上的通敌合作。

entries.definition: To do what is asked or needed for a shared aim; it stresses willingness rather than shared creation.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标做被请求或需要的事；侧重「愿意配合」，而非共同创造。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for joining forces, usually for a specific occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指合在一起干，通常为某件具体的事。

entries.definition: A phrase for combining strength, often against a common opponent or problem.
entries.definitionCN: 指把力量合起来，常针对共同的对手或难题。

entries.definition: To work together in secret for a dishonest purpose; the negative intent is built into the word.
entries.definitionCN: 为不正当目的暗中串通；负面意图已含在词里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare 'work': two people at one bench.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 laborare「劳动」：两个人共用一张工作台。

normal.en: The family runs collaborate, collaboration, collaborator, collaborative, collaborationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 collaborate、collaboration、collaborator、collaborative、collaborationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases ask who and what: collaborate with a team, collaborate on a study.
normal.cn: 固定搭配问「和谁、做什么」：与团队合作、就一项研究合作。

normal.en: The wartime sense is always marked: collaborate with the enemy.
normal.cn: 战时的义项总带标记：与敌人合作。

normal.en: The relative elaborate drops the togetherness and keeps only the working out.
normal.cn: 近形的 elaborate 去掉了「共同」，只留下「做细做透」。

abstract.en: Picture two pairs of hands on one loom, each minding half the threads.
abstract.cn: 想象两双手在同一架织机上，各管一半的线。

abstract.en: Picture two ladders leaning against the same wall so that either can be climbed.
abstract.cn: 想象两架梯子靠在同一面墙上，哪一架都能上。

abstract.en: Picture one rope pulled by four people who never speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳由四个人拉着，始终没有人说话。

examples.en: The poet collaborated with a translator for nearly a decade.
examples.cn: 这位诗人与一位译者合作了将近十年。

examples.en: Local guides collaborated with the survey team throughout the summer.
examples.cn: 当地向导整个夏天都在配合勘测队。

examples.en: Anyone who collaborated with the occupiers was barred from office.
examples.cn: 凡与占领当局合作者都被禁止担任公职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「col（共同）+ labor（劳动）+ ate」——一起干活 → 合作

root: 拉丁 collaborare「一起劳作」= com-（共同）+ laborare（劳动），labor 更深来源不确定；十九世纪进入英语，二十世纪四十年代因战时用法带上「通敌」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe two parties at one bench, but the bench changes: a lab, a studio, a hospital, an occupied country, a fraud, an inquiry, a market and a network.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「两方共用一张工作台」，只是这张台子会换：实验室、工作室、医院、被占领的国家、一桩诈骗、一场调查、一个市场、一张网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pairs of hands working one loom, each responsible for half the threads.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手在同一架织机上操作，各自负责一半的线。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL CENTRE: shared work, and plain cooperation with a request.
branches.cn: 中性地带：共同的工作，以及平常地配合一项请求。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF JOINT PRODUCT: a work of art, and a programme run by institutions.
branches.cn: 两种共同产物：一件艺术作品，与一个由机构运行的项目。

branches.en: THE DARK SIDE: helping an occupier, and helping a fraud.
branches.cn: 暗面：帮助占领者，以及帮助一桩诈骗。

branches.en: RIVALS AT ONE BENCH: competition does not stop cooperation on shared ground.
branches.cn: 对手同桌：竞争并不妨碍在共同地带合作。

branches.en: MACHINES AT ONE BENCH: the human verb reaches software and equipment.
branches.cn: 机器同桌：这个属人的动词延伸到了软件与设备。

intro.en: Collaborate is a Latin compound verb whose prefix and root still build English words, so the whole family reads morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: collaborate 是一个拉丁复合动词，其前缀与词根至今仍在构成英语词，因此整个词族可以按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin laborare gives labor, elaborate and laboratory, while com- adds the sense of doing something with others.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 laborare 衍生 labor、elaborate 与 laboratory，而 com- 增添「与他人一起」之意。

items.example: The prefix makes the labour shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使劳动成为共享的。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of work.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「劳作」的意思。

items.example: The teams collaborate on the survey.
items.exampleCN: 各团队合作开展勘测。

items.example: The collaboration lasted four years.
items.exampleCN: 这次合作持续了四年。

items.meaning: a person who works with others
items.example: Her collaborator wrote the second chapter.
items.exampleCN: 她的合作者写了第二章。

items.example: The project was collaborative from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目从一开始就是协作式的。

items.example: The report was written collaboratively.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告是协作写成的。

items.meaning: one who cooperates with an enemy
items.example: The court tried the collaborationists first.
items.exampleCN: 法庭先审判通敌者。

items.example: The work took a season of labor.
items.exampleCN: 这项工作耗去一季的辛劳。

items.example: She elaborated the plan in an appendix.
items.exampleCN: 她在附录里细化了这个方案。

definition_zh: 合伙；伙伴关系；合伙企业；（体育）搭档关系
definition_en: a business or working relationship between partners, or the state of being partners in an activity
core_image: 两人共用一张工作台，任何一个抽屉都能被其中任何一人拉开
scene: 店门口的木牌上刻着两个姓氏，中间没有分隔符。The two firms formed a partnership to bid for the bridge contract.
sceneCN: 这里 partnership 指「两个主体共同出资、共同承担的合作关系」（第 1 个义项：商业上的合伙）；句意为两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。可辨识物件：木牌、两个姓氏、投标文件、模型桥。

pos.zh: 合伙；合伙企业；伙伴关系

senses.title: A firm owned by partners
senses.definition: a business in which two or more people share ownership, profits and liability
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或更多人共同拥有、共享利润并共担责任的企业
senses.example: The two firms formed a partnership to bid for the bridge contract.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。
senses.why: the noun ending -ship marks a state or a body, so partner plus -ship can name the firm itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾 -ship 标记一种状态或一个团体，因此 partner 加 -ship 可以直接命名这家企业。

senses.title: The relationship of partners
senses.definition: the working relation between people who share an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 共同经营一项事业的人之间的工作关系
senses.example: Their partnership survived two failed ventures.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的合伙关系在两次失败的项目之后仍然存续。
senses.why: the same ending can name the bond rather than the body, which is why the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾既可以命名「关系」，也可以命名「团体」，因此这个词同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: Cooperation between organizations
senses.definition: a formal working arrangement between bodies that remain separate
senses.definitionCN: 各自独立的两方之间正式的工作安排
senses.example: The city entered a partnership with the railway company.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府与铁路公司建立了合作关系。
senses.why: modern usage loosened the legal core: two bodies can be partners without merging.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法松开了法律内核：两个机构不必合并也可以称伙伴。

senses.title: Two batters at one wicket
senses.titleCN: 板球中同时在场的一对击球手
senses.definition: in cricket, the pair batting together and the runs they add
senses.definitionCN: 板球中同时在场的两名击球手，以及他们共同取得的分数
senses.example: Their opening partnership added ninety runs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开局搭档贡献了九十分。
senses.why: sport borrows the word for any pair that must cover for each other on the field.
senses.whyCN: 体育借这个词指任何在场上必须替对方补位的一对。

senses.title: A pairing at the card table
senses.definition: in card games, the pair who play as a team against other pairs
senses.definitionCN: 牌戏中作为一队对抗其他各对的两个人
senses.example: They have been a partnership at bridge for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在桥牌上做搭档已经三十年。
senses.why: a card pair must trust the other's unseen hand, which is partnership in its purest social form.
senses.whyCN: 一对牌手必须信赖对方看不见的牌，这是「合伙」最纯粹的社会形态。

senses.title: Shared responsibility in policy
senses.definition: an arrangement in which government, employers and workers share duties
senses.definitionCN: 政府、雇主与劳动者分担责任的一种安排
senses.example: The wage deal rested on a social partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工资协议建立在社会伙伴关系之上。
senses.why: politics uses the word for duties shared across sectors, where no contract binds the parties.
senses.whyCN: 政治用这个词指跨部门分担的责任，那里并没有合同约束各方。

senses.title: A legally recognised couple
senses.definition: a civil partnership giving a couple rights similar to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 给予一对伴侣类似婚姻权利的民事伴侣关系
senses.example: The law allowed a civil partnership from that year.
senses.exampleCN: 从那一年起，法律允许登记民事伴侣关系。
senses.why: the word spread from commerce to domestic life because both rest on a formal sharing of assets and duties.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从商业扩展到家庭生活，因为两者都建立在正式共享财产与责任之上。

senses.title: A coalition of parties
senses.definition: a governing arrangement between political parties that share power
senses.definitionCN: 分享权力的政党之间的执政安排
senses.example: The coalition called itself a partnership of equals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合政府自称是平等者之间的伙伴关系。
senses.why: coalitions borrow the commercial word to sound voluntary, since no party was bought.
senses.whyCN: 联合政府借用商业词，是为了听起来出于自愿，因为并没有哪一党被买下。

intro.en: Partnership is partner plus -ship, an Old English ending for a state or a body. Partner came from Old French parçonier, a sharer, from Latin partitio 'a division'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: partnership 是 partner 加 -ship 构成，后者是古英语中表示状态或团体的词尾。partner 来自古法语 parçonier「分有者」，源头是拉丁 partitio「分割」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pars meant 'a part, a share'. From it come partition, particle and the whole family of English part words.
items.cn: pars 意为「一部分、一份」。partition、particle 以及英语中整个 part 词族都由此而来。

items.en: Partitio, from partire 'to divide', named a dividing or a share, and Old French turned it into parçon.
items.cn: partitio 出自 partire「分割」，命名分割或所分得的一份，古法语把它变成 parçon。

items.en: Parçonier meant 'a sharer, one who has a part', and English borrowed it as partner in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: parçonier 意为「分有者、占一份的人」，英语在十三世纪以 partner 的形式借入。

items.en: The Old English ending -scipe marked state or condition, as in friendship and lordship; added to partner it made partnership around 1400.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -scipe 标记状态或情形，如 friendship 与 lordship；加在 partner 上，约在十五世纪初形成 partnership。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word hardened into a legal form of business, with deeds, liability and dissolution.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词固化为一种法律上的企业形式，有了契约、责任与解散程序。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first citation of partnership varies between dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of pars is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对 partnership 最早的用例说法不一；pars 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words on the same part root or on confusing near-forms; group two holds nouns for people or bodies that work as one.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「部分」词根、或形近易混的词；第二组收表示「作为一体运作的人或团体」的名词。

entries.definition: From Latin partitio: a division or a dividing screen, which is the physical act of what partnership shares.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 partitio：分割或隔板，正是 partnership 所「分有」的那个动作本身。

entries.definition: From Italian parte, a faction: a committed supporter of one side, sharing the root but not the mutual duty.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 parte「派别」：某一方的坚定支持者，同根，却不含相互的责任。

entries.definition: A sharer in an enterprise; partnership is the state or the body formed by such sharers.
entries.definitionCN: 共同经营中的分有者；partnership 则是由这些分有者形成的状态或团体。

entries.definition: A rarer form with co-, used mostly in older commercial writing for the same arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 加 co- 的较罕形式，多见于较早的商业文书，指同一种安排。

entries.definition: A union of separate parties for a purpose; it stresses remaining separate more than sharing ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种目的把各自独立的两方联合起来；更强调「仍然分开」，而非共享所有权。

entries.definition: A single business project shared by two firms; a partnership may run many projects over years.
entries.definitionCN: 两家公司共担的单一商业项目；而 partnership 可能持续多年、涵盖多个项目。

entries.definition: A separate legal entity; partners are personally liable, which a company's owners are not.
entries.definitionCN: 独立的法律实体；合伙人承担个人责任，而公司的所有者不承担。

entries.definition: A group of people organized around a shared interest; it need not trade or share profit.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕共同兴趣组织起来的一群人；它不必经商，也不必分利。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Partner plus -ship, the ending that turns a person into a state or a body.
normal.cn: partner 加 -ship，后者把一个人变成一种状态或一个团体。

normal.en: The family runs partner, partnership, partnering, partnered, copartnership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 partner、partnership、partnering、partnered、copartnership。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: enter into partnership, dissolve a partnership.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：结成合伙、解散合伙。

normal.en: The partner root means a share, so a partnership is literally a sharing.
normal.cn: partner 的词根意为「一份」，所以 partnership 字面上就是「分有」。

normal.en: Sport and cards keep older senses alive: a batting partnership, a bridge partnership.
normal.cn: 体育与牌戏让较早的义项存活：击球搭档、桥牌搭档。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden sign with two surnames and no separator.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木牌上刻着两个姓氏，中间没有分隔符。

abstract.en: Picture one drawer that either of two people can open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，两个人里任何一个都能拉开。

abstract.en: Picture a boat rowed by two oars that must enter the water together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船由两支桨划动，两支桨必须同时入水。

examples.en: The partnership was dissolved after the senior partner retired.
examples.cn: 资深合伙人退休后，这份合伙关系解散了。

examples.en: The museum works in partnership with three local schools.
examples.cn: 博物馆与三所本地学校合作。

examples.en: Their partnership at the card table lasted longer than their marriage.
examples.cn: 他们在牌桌上的搭档关系，比他们的婚姻还长久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「partner（伙伴）+ ship（状态）」——伙伴所处的那个状态 → 合伙关系

root: partner（古法语 parçonier「分有者」，源自拉丁 pars「部分」、partitio「分割」）+ -ship（古英语 -scipe，表状态或团体），约十五世纪初成词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe people who hold parts of one thing together: a firm, a bond, two organizations, a batting pair, a card pair, a policy deal, a legal couple and a coalition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「共同持有一件事的各一份」的人：一家企业、一段关系、两个机构、一对击球手、一对牌手、一份政策约定、一对法律伴侣，以及一个联合政府。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one workbench shared by two people, with every drawer open to either of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人共用一张工作台，每只抽屉对两人都敞开。

branches.en: THE FIRM AND THE BOND: the body that owns, and the relation that holds it together.
branches.cn: 企业与其纽带：拥有它的团体，以及把它维系住的关系。

branches.en: ORGANIZATIONS AND POLICY: bodies cooperate, and government shares duties with industry.
branches.cn: 机构与政策：机构之间合作，政府与产业分担责任。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE TABLE: a batting pair and a card pair, where trust is physical.
branches.cn: 球场与牌桌：一对击球手与一对牌手，信任在那里是身体性的。

branches.en: A LEGAL COUPLE: the commercial word enters domestic law.
branches.cn: 法律上的伴侣：商业词进入了家庭法。

branches.en: A COALITION: parties call their power-sharing a partnership of equals.
branches.cn: 联合政府：各党把自己的分权安排称作平等者之间的伙伴关系。

intro.en: Partnership combines a French noun of sharing with an Old English ending for a state, which is why it can name both a firm and a relation.
intro.cn: partnership 把一个法语「分有」名词与一个古英语「状态」词尾合在一起，因此它既能命名企业，也能命名关系。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars 'part' yields part, partition and particle, and the French derivative parçonier gives English partner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pars「部分」衍生 part、partition 与 particle，其法语派生词 parçonier 给出英语的 partner。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a share.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「一份」的意思。

items.example: The noun named the act of dividing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名「分割」这一动作。

items.example: The French word became English partner.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语词变成了英语的 partner。

items.example: Each partner signed the deed.
items.exampleCN: 每位合伙人都签了契约。

items.example: The ending turns a person into a relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把一个人变成一种关系。

items.example: The partnership lasted ten years.
items.exampleCN: 这份合伙持续了十年。

items.meaning: the act of joining as partners
items.example: Partnering with local firms came first.
items.exampleCN: 首先是与本地公司结成伙伴。

items.example: The school is partnered with a museum.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校与一家博物馆结对。

items.example: The old deed used copartnership.

definition_zh: 陪伴；伙伴情谊；同伴关系
definition_en: the state of having someone with you, or the friendly relation between companions
core_image: 长椅另一端坐着一个人，不说话，也没有起身离开
scene: 冬夜的候车室里，两个人隔着一个座位坐着，各自看书，谁也没有先走。After his wife died, the old dog's companionship kept him from withdrawing entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 companionship 指「有人在身边所带来的那种陪伴」（第 2 个义项：陪伴带来的慰藉）；句意为妻子去世之后，那条老狗的陪伴使他没有把自己完全封闭起来。可辨识物件：候车室的排椅、两本书、旧狗、暖风机。

senses.title: The state of having someone with you
senses.definition: the condition of not being alone because another person is present
senses.definitionCN: 因为有另一个人在场，而不处于独处的状态
senses.example: He missed the companionship of the workshop more than the work itself.
senses.exampleCN: 他想念作坊里有人做伴，胜过想念那份活儿。
senses.why: companion plus -ship names a state, and this is the plainest one: another body in the room.
senses.whyCN: companion 加 -ship 命名一种状态，这是最朴素的一种：屋里有另一个人的身体在。

senses.title: Comfort drawn from company
senses.definition: the emotional support that comes from having another being near
senses.definitionCN: 因为另一个生命就在近旁而得到的情感支撑
senses.example: After his wife died, the old dog's companionship kept him from withdrawing entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 妻子去世之后，那条老狗的陪伴使他没有把自己完全封闭起来。
senses.why: the state sense turns inward here: what matters is not presence but what presence does to the heart.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把「状态」转向内心：要紧的不是有人在，而是「有人在」对心做了什么。

senses.title: The bond between companions
senses.definition: the friendly relation that grows between people who spend time together
senses.definitionCN: 相处日久的人之间生长出来的友好关系
senses.example: Years of companionship made silence between them easy.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的相伴让他们之间的沉默变得自在。
senses.why: the noun can name the relation rather than the state, which is why it appears in writing about long friendships.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可以命名「关系」而非「状态」，因此常出现在写长久友谊的文字里。

senses.title: Ordinary days done together
senses.definition: the shared routine of daily tasks with another person, rather than any special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人共同承担日常事务的那种常规，而非某个特别场合
senses.example: It was the companionship of the morning walk, not the talk, that she remembered.
senses.exampleCN: 她记得的是早晨散步时的那份相伴，而不是那些谈话。
senses.why: the noun also covers the unremarkable repetition of shared days, which is where companionship is usually built.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也覆盖「共同度过的日子」那种不起眼的重复，而陪伴通常正是在那里筑成。

senses.title: Pet companionship
senses.definition: the company provided by a domestic animal kept for that purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为作伴而饲养的家养动物所提供的陪伴
senses.example: Many clinics now prescribe companionship as well as medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 许多诊所如今既开药，也建议养宠物作伴。
senses.why: the word does not require a speaker, so an animal can fill the companion role without any conversation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词并不要求对方会说话，因此动物不必交谈也能填补「同伴」这个位置。

senses.title: Fellowship in a group
senses.definition: the shared ease of people who belong to the same body or trade
senses.definitionCN: 属于同一团体或行业的人之间那种共享的自在
senses.example: The guild offered companionship as much as training.
senses.exampleCN: 行会所提供的，除了训练，还有同伴情谊。
senses.why: a group supplies the same warmth as one friend, and English extends the singular noun to the collective.
senses.whyCN: 一个团体提供与一个朋友同样的温度，英语把这个单数名词扩展到集体上。

senses.title: Paid presence
senses.definition: company provided as a service, often to elderly or isolated people
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种服务提供的陪伴，常给老人或孤立的人
senses.example: The agency advertises companionship, not nursing care.
senses.exampleCN: 这家机构宣传的是陪伴，而非护理。
senses.why: once companionship can be hired, the word separates the presence from the affection that usually comes with it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦陪伴可以被雇来，这个词就把「在场」与通常随之而来的情感分开了。

senses.title: Company in old age
senses.definition: the particular comfort of not growing old alone
senses.definitionCN: 不在孤独中老去的那种特别安慰
senses.example: The home matched residents for companionship rather than for care.
senses.exampleCN: 这家养老院按「能不能作伴」而不是按护理需求来配对住户。
senses.why: ageing narrows the general sense to the one place where presence matters most.
senses.whyCN: 年老把一般意义收窄到「在场」最重要的那个场合。

intro.en: Companionship is companion plus -ship. Companion came from Old French compagnon, from Late Latin companionem, 'one who shares bread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: companionship 是 companion 加 -ship 构成。companion 来自古法语 compagnon，源头是晚期拉丁 companionem「同吃面包的人」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Panis meant 'bread'. It survives in English pantry and in the company of the Latin compound that built companion.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」。它留存于英语的 pantry，也留在构成 companion 的那个拉丁复合词里。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus panis produced companio, 'one who eats bread with another', a messmate rather than a friend.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 panis 得出 companio「与他人同吃面包的人」，是同席吃饭的人，而非朋友。

items.en: Old French compagnon carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, by then meaning any person who goes along with another.
items.cn: 古法语 compagnon 在十三世纪把这个词带入英语，当时已指任何与另一人同行的人。

items.en: The Old English ending -scipe formed nouns of state, as in friendship; companion plus -ship named the condition rather than the person.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -scipe 构成表状态的名词，如 friendship；companion 加 -ship 命名的是状态，而不是人。

items.en: In modern use the word covers friendly company, animal company and paid presence, and it appears in medicine and in care policy.
items.cn: 在现代用法里，这个词涵盖友伴、动物作伴以及受雇的陪伴，并出现在医学与照护政策中。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of companionship is dated differently across dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of panis is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对 companionship 最早的用例说法不一；panis 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words on the same bread-sharing root or on similar shapes; group two holds nouns for being with others, each with a different warmth.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「同吃面包」词根、或形近的词；第二组收表示「与人在一起」的名词，温度各不相同。

entries.definition: The person; companionship is the state or relation that person creates.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个人；companionship 则是这个人所造出的状态或关系。

entries.definition: From the same bread-sharing root, but it means presence in general, and also a business firm.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「同吃面包」词根，但意为一般的「有人在场」，也指一家公司。

entries.definition: The verb: to go along with someone, or to occur together with something.
entries.definitionCN: 同族动词：陪某人同行，或与某物同时发生。

entries.definition: From Latin campus 'field' through Italian campagna: a military or political drive, with no link to bread or company.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语 campagna 出自拉丁 campus「田野」：军事或政治行动，与面包、陪伴无关。

entries.definition: A relation of mutual affection; companionship can exist with much less feeling attached.
entries.definitionCN: 相互喜爱的感情关系；companionship 可以在情感少得多的情况下存在。

entries.definition: The friendly feeling among members of a group; it is collective where companionship is often one-to-one.
entries.definitionCN: 团体成员之间的友好气氛；它是集体的，而 companionship 常是一对一的。

entries.definition: The fact of being in a place; it carries no warmth, which companionship always implies somewhat.
entries.definitionCN: 身在某处这一事实；它不带温度，而 companionship 多少总带一点。

entries.definition: The state of being alone, sometimes chosen and sometimes suffered; it is what companionship removes or relieves.
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，有时自愿，有时被迫；companionship 所消除或缓解的正是它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus panis 'bread': the one you share bread with.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 panis「面包」：与你分吃面包的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs companion, companionship, companionable, company, accompany.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 companion、companionship、companionable、company、accompany。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name who and what kind: human companionship, the companionship of animals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配点明对象与种类：人的陪伴、动物的陪伴。

normal.en: The word is usually uncountable, since a state is not counted like objects.
normal.cn: 这个词通常不可数，因为状态不像物件那样可以计数。

normal.en: The near form campaign comes from a word for field, not from bread.
normal.cn: 近形的 campaign 出自「田野」一词，而不是「面包」。

abstract.en: Picture a bench with a second person at the far end who does not get up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长椅，另一端坐着一个人，始终没有起身。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps burning in one room, neither lighting the other.
abstract.cn: 想象同一间屋里点着两盏灯，谁也不照谁。

abstract.en: Picture a table laid for two though only one plate is used.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆了两人份的桌子，却只用了一只盘子。

examples.en: The long walk was easier for the companionship of a neighbour.
examples.cn: 有邻居作伴，那段长路好走了许多。

examples.en: She valued the companionship of the reading group more than the books.
examples.cn: 相比书，她更看重读书会里那份相伴。

examples.en: Companionship of any kind was what the ward lacked most.
examples.cn: 这间病房最缺的，就是任何一种陪伴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「companion（同伴）+ ship（状态）」——同伴在旁的那种状态 → 陪伴

root: companion（古法语 compagnon，晚期拉丁 companionem「同吃面包的人」= com- 共同 + panis 面包）+ -ship（古英语 -scipe，表状态）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe another being nearby: a state, a comfort, a bond, a pet, a guild, a hired presence and the particular company of old age.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「另一个生命就在近旁」：一种状态、一份慰藉、一段情谊、一只动物、一个行会、一份受雇的在场，以及晚年那种特别的相伴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench with a second person at the far end who does not stand up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长椅，另一端坐着一个人，始终没有起身。

branches.en: PRESENCE AND ITS EFFECT: someone is there, and that presence steadies the heart.
branches.cn: 在场与其作用：有人在，而这份在场把心稳住。

branches.en: THE BOND AND THE BODY: one friendship deepened, and a whole guild's shared ease.
branches.cn: 纽带与团体：一段加深的友谊，以及整个行会共享的自在。

branches.en: COMPANIONS THAT DO NOT SPEAK: an animal fills the role without a word.
branches.cn: 不说话的同伴：动物不必说一个字，也能填上这个位置。

branches.en: PRESENCE FOR HIRE: the word splits company from affection.
branches.cn: 受雇的在场：这个词把「陪伴」与「情感」分开。

branches.en: OLD AGE: the general state narrows to the years when it matters most.
branches.cn: 晚年：一般性的状态收窄到最需要它的那些年。

intro.en: Companionship joins a French noun meaning bread-sharer to an Old English ending for state, so the whole word can be read as 'the condition of sharing bread'.
intro.cn: companionship 把一个意为「分吃面包者」的法语名词与一个古英语「状态」词尾合在一起，整词可以读作「分吃面包的情形」。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis 'bread' is the root of the compound, and French and English endings do the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 panis「面包」是这个复合词的词根，其余由法语与英语的词尾完成。

items.example: The prefix makes the bread shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使面包成为共享的。

items.example: The root names the shared loaf.
items.exampleCN: 词根点名那只共享的面包。

items.example: The Latin noun began as a table word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词起初是餐桌上的词。

items.example: The companion walked beside her.
items.exampleCN: 同伴走在她身旁。

items.example: The ending turns a person into a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把一个人变成一种状态。

items.example: Companionship eased the winter.
items.exampleCN: 陪伴让冬天好过些。

items.example: He was companionable without being talkative.
items.exampleCN: 他很好相处，却不多话。

items.meaning: the state of being with others
items.example: She kept him company.
items.exampleCN: 她陪着他。

items.example: A nurse accompanied the patient.
items.exampleCN: 一名护士陪同病人。
